role.title: Manufacturing Execution Systems Senior Manager
role.description:
Ready to join a global leader in air movement and ventilation? At Greenheck Group, joining our team means more than just starting a job, it’s joining an award-winning culture prioritizing your growth and development. Our unwavering commitment in supporting our team members both personally and professionally has earned us national recognition time and time again. As an innovative, environmentally responsible manufacturer of commercial HVAC systems, Greenheck Group designs and manufactures industry-leading air movement and ventilation solutions through our family of trusted brands. Our products are found in commercial, institutional, and industrial facilities worldwide, from schools and hospitals to factories and stadiums. Since 1947, we’ve proudly invested in our people and our communities, fostering innovation, leadership, and opportunity at every level. We are more than products, we are a team of inspired people doing extraordinary things.

As a Manufacturing Execution Systems Senior Manager for Greenheck Group you will own product strategy and delivery across Greenheck Group’s full manufacturing-systems portfolio — Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), maintenance management, machine integration, machine/production monitoring (MDC), and automation. You will serve as the senior product leader for Manufacturing Execution Systems, directly leading the MES functional lead team, owning the roadmap for the Critical Manufacturing platform consolidation, and establishing enterprise standards and consistency for manufacturing technology across Greenheck Group’s plants. You will operate as the critical connective link between enterprise manufacturing systems and the business, IT, Divisional Systems teams, and the broader Operational Systems/CoE community.

**WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING**

* Program Leadership: Own the product roadmap and delivery across the full manufacturing-systems portfolio — MES, maintenance management, machine integration, machine/production monitoring (MDC), and automation — across all Greenheck production sites. Lead the end-to-end roadmap for the Critical Manufacturing platform consolidation, replacing legacy custom integrations and MII applications across Greenheck's production sites. Coordinate cross-functional teams, allocate resources, and co-manage project timelines with Program Management. Drive accountability throughout execution and establish aggressive, results-oriented goals for the team.
* Divisional & CoE Alignment: Serve as the critical point of alignment between enterprise MES capabilities and divisional/plant-level execution — partnering closely with the business, IT, Divisional Systems teams, and the other Operational Systems/CoE groups (e.g., Operational Excellence, Machine Automation/MDC) to ensure enterprise standards translate into plant-level adoption and results.
* Team Leadership: Build and lead the MES functional lead team across the MES, maintenance, machine integration, monitoring, and automation domains.
* Change Leadership: Facilitate organizational change related to MES and manufacturing-systems adoption; communicate to create buy-in and promote system acceptance across plant floors.
* Standards and Consistency: Drive manufacturing-systems standards and consistency across Greenheck production sites through an MES steering committee and governance framework spanning MES, maintenance, machine integration, monitoring, and automation.
* Communication: Provide status updates on timeline, cost, and risk to the Operational Systems and OT Executive Steering Committees; communicate with team, stakeholders, and senior/executive leaders.
* Strategic Planning: Set the vision and develop and execute a comprehensive manufacturing-systems strategy aligned with organizational goals; identify opportunities for process improvement, efficiency gains, and cost reduction across MES, maintenance, machine integration, monitoring, and automation.
* Collaboration: Work closely with the Sr Manager, ERP and Program/Project Management on shared roadmap, resourcing, and delivery dependencies; partner with external resources to ensure manufacturing systems align with business objectives.
* Best Practices: Stay current on MES, automation, and manufacturing-technology trends and bring forward platform recommendations.

**WHAT YOU SHOULD HAVE AS A MANUFACTURING EXECUTION SYSTEMS SENIOR MANAGER**

* 4 Year / bachelor’s degree in engineering, information systems, business, or a related field required
* Graduate Degree in engineering, information systems, or related field preferred
* 4-6 years of relevant work experience in MES implementation, project management or related fields required
* Strong understanding of manufacturing processes and production environments required
* Certification in project management preferred
* Experience with MES systems and their integration with ERP preferred
* 80/20 thinking
* Manufacturing experience and credibility
* Strong team building and leadership
* Systems and technology savvy
* Strategic thinking and leadership
* Action-oriented

**SOME THINGS WE THINK YOU SHOULD KNOW**

* Travel of 10 to 25% will be required for this role.
* This is an on-site role at our Schofield, WI location.

**COMPENSATION & BENEFITS**

Greenheck Group takes pride in providing competitive total compensation along with a comprehensive benefits package as part of our total rewards program. The compensation for this role includes base salary along with the opportunity to earn additional variable compensation based on achieving specific performance metrics. The starting base pay range for this position is $160,353 - $198,083 and may vary based on factors such as job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and performance.

 

With best-in-class benefits, you can be the best you, and together, we can be the best in the industry. Visit our **Perks & Benefits page** for more information on these offerings:

 

* Health & Family Support
* Financial Security
* Learning & Development
* Rewards & Recognition
* Wellbeing & Mental Health
* Work-Life Balance
* Fun Perks

**SPECIAL NOTATION**

The preceding statements are intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by people in this position. They are not intended to be construed as an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills. The Employer retains the right to change or assign other duties to this position.

**PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS**

Work is performed in an office environment and requires the ability to operate standard office equipment, such as a computer and phone. Sedentary work. Exerting up to 10 pounds of force occasionally and/or negligible amount of force frequently or constantly to lift, carry, push, pull or otherwise move objects. Repetitive motion. Substantial motions of the wrists, hands, and/or fingers. The person is required to have close visual acuity to perform an activity such as: preparing and analyzing data, and figures; transcribing; viewing a computer terminal; extensive reading. Occasional mobility required to attend in-person meetings and complete various office tasks.

**EEO STATEMENT**

We are an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or veteran status.

**ACCOMMODATIONS REQUEST**

Greenheck Group complies with federal and state disability laws and makes reasonable accommodations for applicants and candidates with disabilities. To request an accommodation for the application or interview process, please email HR@greenheck.com with your name, job title, posting number, and requested accommodation.

**RECRUITING FRAUD ALERT**

At Greenheck Group, your personal information and online safety are our top priorities. Our recruiters will only direct candidates to apply through our official career page at https://greenheckgroup.com/careers/. We will never request payments, financial account details, or sensitive information such as Social Security numbers. If you’re unsure about the legitimacy of a message, please contact HR@greenheck.com for verification.

If you're looking for a place to grow while working with happy, enthusiastic, values-based people, you'll enjoy your career with us!

role.title: Senior Manager Operations
role.description:
Since 2018, Elevate Aircraft Seating has been enhancing the passenger experience through innovative aircraft seat design and manufacturing. With locations in California, Washington, and Germany we are guided by creativity, collaboration, and a shared commitment to quality.

We are looking for a skilled Senior Manager Operations to join our team in Santa Maria, CA. This is an on-site position based in Santa Maria, CA. We value teamwork, inclusivity, and continuous professional development, and we offer competitive benefits along with opportunities for growth.

**Export Control Requirements:**

**This position must meet U.S. export control compliance requirements. To meet U.S. export control compliance requirements, a “U.S. Person” as defined by 22 C.F.R. §120.62 is required. “U.S. Person” includes U.S. Citizen, U.S. National, lawful permanent resident, refugee, or asylee.**

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Senior Manager, Operations is responsible for leading and overseeing manufacturing operations and maintenance activities to ensure the achievement of safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost objectives. This role drives operational performance through effective resource planning, workforce development, and process optimization while supporting continuous improvement initiatives. Partnering cross-functionally, the Senior Manager implements operational strategies, promotes accountability, and ensures efficient manufacturing execution aligned with organizational and customer objectives.

**SUMMARY OF JOB DUTIES** - **Essential Functions****(Other duties and projects may be assigned or requested.)**

*Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions*

**Operational Leadership & Performance**

* Lead and oversee daily manufacturing operations and maintenance activities to achieve safety, quality, on-time delivery, productivity, labor efficiency, scrap reduction, and work-in-process (WIP) inventory objectives.
* Establish, monitor, and drive accountability for key operational performance indicators (KPIs), implementing corrective actions to address performance gaps.
* Support continuous improvement initiatives by identifying operational inefficiencies, collaborating with relevant stakeholders, and implementing improvements within manufacturing operations.

**Production Planning & Execution**

* Oversee all phases of manufacturing operations to ensure production activities comply with established procedures, quality standards, and approved manufacturing processes.
* Plan, coordinate, and optimize departmental activities, production schedules, and resource allocation to meet customer requirements and business objectives.
* Evaluate production capacity, workforce requirements, and operational constraints to ensure effective utilization of labor, equipment, and manufacturing resources.

**People Leadership & Workforce Development**

* Lead, develop, and manage production and associated functional teams, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and operational excellence.
* Oversee workforce planning, recruitment, onboarding, training, and employee development to maintain operational readiness.
* Establish performance expectations, evaluate employee performance, and partner with Human Resources on coaching, employee relations, corrective actions, and performance management.

**Quality, Safety & Regulatory Compliance**

* Ensure manufacturing operations adhere to established Quality Management System (QMS) requirements, AS9100 standards, applicable aerospace regulations, and internal policies and procedures.
* Promote a culture of safety, quality, and compliance by ensuring employees are appropriately trained and consistently follow established manufacturing procedures.

**Financial Management & Cross-Functional Collaboration**

* Manage departmental budgets, monitor operational expenditures, and implement cost-control measures to support financial objectives.
* Partner with Supply Chain, Planning, Quality, Engineering, Program Management, and other stakeholders to resolve operational challenges, align production priorities, and meet customer delivery commitments.

**Other**

* Maintain a safe, secure and legal work environment, adhering to all Company policies and procedures.
* Protect the confidentiality of the Company’s information and products.
* Contribute to team efforts by performing other job-related duties and projects as assigned or requested.

**GENERAL QUALIFICATIONS – Education, Knowledge, and Experience**

**Education**:

* High School Diploma or GED equivalent required.
* Associate degree, technical/trade certification, or bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing, Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field preferred.

**Experience**:

* 10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including 5+ years in a leadership role overseeing production teams, operational performance, and manufacturing processes.
* Demonstrated success managing manufacturing operations in a complex, quality-driven production environment, with a focus on improving safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost performance.
* Proven ability to lead supervisors or managers, develop high-performing teams, and drive operational improvements across multiple manufacturing functions.

**Skills**:

* Strong leadership and people management skills, with the ability to develop teams, establish accountability, and manage employee performance.
* Proficiency in manufacturing operations, production planning, workforce allocation, and capacity management.
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to interpret operational KPIs and implement effective corrective actions.
* Knowledge of budget management, cost control, and resource optimization within a manufacturing environment.
* Effective communication, organizational, and cross-functional collaboration skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and support business objectives.

**Preferred Skills/Experience:**

* Experience in aerospace manufacturing, aircraft interiors, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments, with knowledge of AS9100 and Quality Management Systems (QMS).
* Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
* Experience utilizing Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems and manufacturing performance reporting tools.

**Other**:

* Extended or irregular hours may be required.
* Must be authorized to work in the United States.
* Elevate Aircraft Seating is an “at-will” employer; employment is at the mutual consent of both the employee and the employer, and may be terminated at will for any reason, with or without cause, at any time during employment with the Company.
* As business conditions warrant a change in the operating necessities of the Company, all employees are expected to react productively, handle other essential tasks assigned now or in the future.
* Tasks may vary slightly based on products produced at a division.
* Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

**CERTIFICATES AND LICENSE**

* N/A

**SUPERVISION PROVIDED TO THE POSITION**

* Direction is provided for assignments in terms of desired outcome (goals), timing and budget.? Work is reviewed or measured in terms of meeting organizational objectives and schedules.

**LEADERSHIP RESPONSIBILITY**

* Provides leadership, coaching, and direction to operational personnel to achieve organizational goals, operational performance objectives, and budgetary targets. Responsible for employee development, performance management, and building organizational capability.

**PROBLEM SOLVING**

* Develop and implement solutions to complex operational challenges that are consistent with organizational objectives and established business practices.

**LANGUAGE SKILLS**

* Ability to communicate effectively in English, both verbally and in writing.

**COMPENSATION & BENEFITS** 
*Elevate Aircraft Seating offers competitive wages and benefits to recognize employees for their work. The base pay offered will vary depending on job-related knowledge, skills, location, experience and take into account internal equity.*

**Salary Range Transparency:** $125,500 - $185,000

**Featured Benefits:**

* Generous 401(K) matching with immediate eligibility and vesting
* 3 weeks of Paid Time Off
* 12 paid holidays
* Affordable health care plans for yourself and your family
* And so much more!

**Other Perks:**

* Supportive workplace environment with a team-oriented culture
* Potential for growth within organization

role.title: Director of Operations Home Health
role.description:
**$10,000 Sign On Bonus for External Candidates**

**Explore opportunities with Amedisys, part of the Optum family of businesses**. We provide home health, hospice and community-based services that help people receive quality care where they feel most comfortable: at home. Rooted in personalized care, we support patients and provide comfort through each stage of their health journey, while building trusted relationships along the way. Find a home for your career here. Join us and embrace a culture of **Caring. Connecting. Growing together**.

The RN Director of Operations is responsible for the overall organization, financial management, and operational leadership of one or more home health care centers. This role provides strategic and operational oversight to ensure regulatory compliance, quality patient care, business growth, fiscal performance, and staff development, while supervising clinical leadership and supporting interdisciplinary care delivery.

**Primary Responsibilities:**

* Handles employment decisions for direct report staff, including decisions to hire, fire, advance, promote or change status
* Responsible for overall organization and financial management of the care center
* Provides supervision to the clinical manager(s) who ensure the delivery of quality care to patients
* Maintains the image of the care center in the community, as well as state and national organizations
* Provides input, guidance and feedback related to marketing activities and care center marketing plan to ensure that goals for growth are met
* Ensures adequate orientation of every team member assigned to their care center
* Assigns and directs staff with appropriate skills to perform duties
* Provides leadership planning for staff education programs, administrative/staff meetings, in services
* Encourages continuous education and staff development for all team members. Sets positive, attainable expectations, objectives and goals for the care center
* Ensures implementation of a performance improvement program to drive quality care, positive patient outcomes, and address negative trends
* Responsible for the delivery of care for all patients served by the care centers by providing supervision and support to the clinical manager
* Other duties as assigned

You'll be rewarded and recognized for your performance in an environment that will challenge you and give you clear direction on what it takes to succeed in your role as well as provide development for other roles you may be interested in.

**Required Qualifications:**

* Associate's degree in business or related in a clinical field
* 2+ years of home care experience and at least one year of supervisory experience or 2+ years of experience in leadership/management in healthcare, home health or hospice

**Preferred Qualifications:**

* Bachelor's degree in business or clinical related field with a current license

role.title: Sr. Director, Operational Excellence
role.description:
Sr. Director, Operational Excellence

**Position Summary**
====================

The Senior Director of Operational Excellence serves as a key strategic and operational partner to the Vice President of Operations, responsible for driving enterprise-wide operational initiatives, workforce optimization, project execution, and organizational effectiveness across CRH Healthcare.

This leader provides direct oversight of the centralized Provider Scheduling team, ensuring effective scheduling operations, proactive coverage planning, workforce utilization, and continuous process improvement. Additionally, the Sr. Director partners with regional and cross-functional leaders to translate strategic priorities into actionable plans, establish accountability, identify operational improvement opportunities, and ensure consistent execution across the organization. The position requires a balance of strategic thinking, hands-on leadership, financial acumen, and the ability to independently drive results in a complex, multi-site healthcare environment.

**Essential Responsibilities**
==============================

**Operational Excellence & Executive Support**
----------------------------------------------

* Serve as a strategic operational partner to the VP of Operations, translating enterprise priorities into actionable execution plans, establishing accountability across functional teams, and ensuring initiatives are delivered on time with measurable operational and financial outcomes.
* Develop and maintain standardized operational performance through reporting that identifies trends, variances, and opportunities across regions. Partner with operational leadership to develop corrective action plans, monitor progress, and ensure sustained improvement.
* Ensure operational excellence with vendors and processes that support the business, including procurement, surveys, and regulatory requirements.
* Support the VP of Operations in evaluating competing priorities, organizational capacity, and resource allocation to ensure alignment with enterprise objectives.
* Develop operational process workflow structure, and communication and training plans to implement, along with feedback loop and tracking to measure success and/or challenge.
* Other duties as assigned by the VP of Operations.

**Workforce Optimization**
--------------------------

* Direct and oversee the centralized Provider Scheduling team, including performance, workload, service expectations and escalation practices.
* Oversee provider scheduling processes, capacity visibility, coverage planning and coordination with regional operational leaders. Identify recurring coverage risks, utilization opportunities and avoidable scheduling disruptions.
* Coordinate with Operational Leadership, Talent Acquisition and Finance on workforce demand, hiring priorities, and labor cost trends.

**Project Management**
----------------------

* Lead full project lifecycle, from planning to closeout for operational initiatives.
* Establish project governance, prioritization, milestones, risks and executive reporting.
* Develop stakeholder engagement, communication, training and adoption plans to sustain operational change.
* Manage project scope, schedules, budgets, and deliverables effectively.

**Qualifications**
==================

* Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business, operations or related field.
* 7+ years of progressive experience in healthcare operations, workforce management, project delivery or operational excellence.
* 5+ years of people leadership experience, including demonstrated success leading managers or functional teams multi-stie environment with a distributed field force.
* Experience supporting multi-site healthcare operations; urgent care or ambulatory care experience preferred.
* Proven ability to lead teams, drive change, influence business partners, and deliver operational results through data-driven decision making, stakeholder collaboration, and organizational influence.
* Strong project portfolio governance, change management, workforce analytics, financial acumen and stakeholder influence.
* Ability to lead through partnerships and remote workforce.
* Office based position with approximately 25% travel to company clinics.

*CRH Healthcare is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made in accordance with applicable federal, state, and local laws. All offers are contingent upon successful completion of applicable credentialing, licensure verification, background review, and employment requirements.*

role.title: Senior Director, Franchise Operations
role.description:
**Job Description Summary:**

**Job Description**

 

The Senior Director Franchise Operations leads the Operations function across the South Region and is responsible for execution of the full portfolio across Coca-Cola United and all South Region Mainstream bottlers, translating aligned business strategies into integrated operating plans, disciplined marketplace execution, and sustainable performance. The role shapes regional operating priorities, recommends resource allocation, and aligns bottler regional operations teams and cross-functional partners to deliver volume, revenue, transactions, share, and profitable growth objectives. The role connects strategic planning with frontline execution, leads the regional performance agenda, and resolves cross-market execution barriers within delegated authority. As the direct people leader of the Franchise Operations team, the Senior Director sets clear accountabilities and develops Directors’ commercial judgment, financial acumen, and general management capabilities. The role partners with commercial, strategy, and transformation leaders to incorporate aligned initiatives into core operating plans without duplicating their functional mandates.

 

**What You’ll Do for Us**

 

* Lead the South Region Franchise Operations performance agenda for the full portfolio across Coca-Cola United and all South Region Mainstream bottlers, driving profitable volume, revenue, transactions, and share growth through clear priorities, integrated operating plans, and accountable execution with bottler partners.

* Expand market potential through Share of Visual Inventory (SOVI), Cold Drink Equipment (CDE), day one minute one innovation execution, and best-in-class conversion of category and commercial plans into outlet-level growth.

* Strengthen bottler operating partnerships by aligning regional, division, and sales-center teams on growth corridors across customers, channels, brands, and packages, securing shared execution commitments through influence rather than direct authority over bottler operations.

* Lead the Franchise Operations contribution to annual and long-range business planning, translating aligned South Region growth priorities into geography-specific operating plans, capability requirements, execution milestones, and measurable business outcomes.

* Assess differences in market potential and performance across bottlers and geographies; recommend operating priorities, resource deployment, and short- and long-term interventions to the VP, and lead implementation of agreed choices.

* Directly lead the Franchise Operations team, setting individual objectives and decision rights, managing performance, and holding Directors accountable for business commitments, bottler partnership, and execution follow-through across their assigned geographies.

* Develop the next generation of franchise leaders through regular coaching, actionable feedback, individual development and succession plans, and cross-functional assignments that build commercial judgment, financial acumen, strategic problem-solving, and general management capabilities while delivering current-role results.

* Lead weekly and monthly regional performance routines, integrating revenue, volume, share, transactions, and execution indicators into clear diagnoses, decisions, named owners, and time-bound actions—not reporting alone.

* Hold Directors accountable for identifying root causes of performance gaps and agreeing corrective actions with bottler regional operations teams; track recovery, adjust plans, and escalate unresolved risks and material trade-offs to the VP with clear recommendations.

* Manage discretionary budgets and deploy resources within approved authority, balancing growth potential, regional business needs, expected returns, and bottler execution capacity; recommend investment trade-offs and additional resource needs

* Lead regional deployment of aligned commercial strategies and growth initiatives, partnering with commercial, strategy, and transformation leaders to establish operational readiness, clear sequencing, ownership, and adoption within core business plans.

* Lead development and activation of contingency plans with bottler and cross-functional partners to protect annual business plan delivery across revenue, volume, share, net outlets, SOVI, and pricing execution; define recovery milestones and monitor results.

* Build execution capability with bottler regional operations teams through targeted training, effective scorecards, and disciplined business routines; identify successful market practices and lead adoption across relevant South Region geographies.

* Partner with franchise commercial leaders to lead the bi-monthly planning process, integrating customer, channel, marketing, finance, and supply-chain inputs into a coherent regional execution agenda with clear priorities and bottler commitments.

Maintain a regular in-market cadence with Directors and bottler regional operations teams to validate outlet execution, learn from frontline teams and customers, and understand execution barriers; bring the voice of the market into regional decisions, capability priorities, and future business plans. 

 

**Qualifications & Requirements**

 

* Bachelor’s degree with a Master’s degree is preferred.

* 10 or more years in a CPG organization across sales, key account, franchise management, or operations, including P&L responsibility, direct people management, and leadership of business execution across multiple geographies.

* Demonstrated success translating annual and long-range strategies into integrated operating plans, forecasting business performance, managing customer and distributor relationships, and leading corrective actions that deliver sustained growth.

* Strong commercial and financial judgment, including experience with revenue and operating P&Ls, investment trade-offs, resource prioritization, selling, and negotiation in a complex franchise or entrepreneurial environment.

* Strong understanding of channel marketing, customer and outlet execution, syndicated research, and competitive analysis, with the ability to combine data and frontline insights to identify growth opportunities and execution priorities.

* Proven ability to lead and develop experienced individual contributors through clear expectations, performance management, coaching, individual development plans, and succession planning.

* The ability to influence outcomes and be persuasive.

The Coca-Cola Company will not offer sponsorship for employment status (including, but not limited to, H1-B visa status and other employment-based nonimmigrant visas) for this position. Accordingly, all applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis and must not require The Coca-Cola Company's sponsorship to continue to work legally in the United States.

**Skills:**

Business Integrations, Business Planning, Channel Management, Execution Excellence, High Impact Communication, Market Dynamics, Negotiation, Revenue Growth Management, Value Chain Economics

**Pay Range:**

United States: 198,000 - 230,000 USD


*Base pay offered may vary depending on geography, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. A full range of medical, financial, and/or other benefits, dependent on the position, is offered.*

**Annual Incentive Reference Value Percentage:**

50

*Annual Incentive reference value is a market-based competitive value for your role. It falls in the middle of the range for your role, indicating performance at target.*

**Long-term Incentive Reference Value Percentage:**

20

*Long-term Incentive reference value is a market-based competitive value for your role.*

**Location(s):**

United States of America

**City/Cities:**

Atlanta

**Travel Required:**

26% - 50%

**Relocation Provided:**

Yes

**Job Posting End Date:**

November 13, 2026

**Our Purpose and Growth Culture:**

We are taking deliberate action to nurture an inclusive culture that is grounded in our company purpose, to refresh the world and make a difference. We act with a growth mindset, take an expansive approach to what’s possible and believe in continuous learning to improve our business and ourselves. We focus on four key behaviors – curious, empowered, inclusive and agile – and value how we work as much as what we achieve. We believe that our culture is one of the reasons our company continues to thrive after 130+ years. Visit Our Purpose and Vision to learn more about these behaviors and how you can bring them to life in your next role at Coca-Cola.

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and do not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class. role.title: Director, Quality Engineering
role.description:
**Become a part of our caring community**
=========================================

Humana is committed to helping people achieve their best health by delivering innovative technology solutions that enable exceptional member and provider experiences. 
The Director, Quality Engineering – Test Data Management (EQE) is a senior technology leader responsible for defining, advancing, and operating Humana's enterprise Test Data Management (TDM) function within Enterprise Quality Engineering. Reporting to the VP, Quality Engineering, this role leads the strategy, operating model, and execution of secure, scalable, compliant, and automation-enabled test data capabilities that support software delivery across Humana's business and technology organizations. 
This leader is accountable for building and leading a high-performing organization responsible for core TDM services, including test data provisioning, synthetic data generation, masking, de-identification, data lifecycle management, and environment data coordination. The Director will partner closely with Quality Engineering, Engineering, Product, Architecture, DevOps, Infrastructure, Security, Privacy, Risk, and Data teams to ensure test data is available, fit for purpose, and aligned to delivery, compliance, and release readiness needs. 
The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in test data management, data engineering, governance, privacy, and automation in a complex enterprise environment. This role will drive modernization of TDM practices through automation-first and AI-enabled capabilities, while establishing standards, controls, and reusable services that improve engineering throughput, reduce delivery friction, and strengthen compliance and data protection across non-production environments.

**Responsibilities**

**Leadership, Strategy & Operating Model**

* Lead the enterprise Test Data Management function within EQE, including strategic direction, operating model execution, and organizational development.
* Build, lead, and develop a high-performing team of managers, engineers, and test data specialists across multiple groups supporting segment and enterprise needs.
* Oversee a distributed organization of **50+ associates** and create clear priorities, role clarity, and performance expectations.
* Partner with Quality Engineering, Engineering, Product, Architecture, DevOps, Infrastructure, Security, and Data teams to align TDM services with business and delivery priorities.
* Drive a scalable support model for segment TDM services across multiple portfolios and delivery teams.
* Promote a culture of quality, compliance, continuous improvement, and shared ownership of secure test data practices.

**Test Data Engineering & Management**

 

* Lead enterprise engineering and management of secure, scalable, and compliant test data solutions.
* Oversee delivery of core TDM capabilities, including:Test data provisioningSynthetic data generationData masking and obfuscationData de-identificationData quality enablementTest data automationData lifecycle managementEnvironment data coordination
* Ensure test data is available, fit for purpose, and aligned to quality engineering, release, and environment needs.
* Advance data engineering practices that improve the reliability, reusability, and speed of test data provisioning across delivery pipelines.
* Support complex testing needs across functional, integration, regression, end-to-end, and non-production validation use cases.

**AI-Enabled & Automation-First TDM**

 

* Drive **AI-enabled** and automation-first TDM strategies to improve speed, intelligence, scalability, and coverage of test data operations.
* Expand the use of AI and advanced automation for synthetic data generation, sensitive data detection, masking rule optimization, provisioning efficiency, and data quality insights.
* Integrate TDM automation into CI/CD and engineering workflows where applicable to reduce manual effort and increase release confidence.
* Partner with enterprise engineering and platform teams to modernize TDM tooling, workflows, and reusable patterns.
* Establish metrics to evaluate automation effectiveness, data readiness, cycle time reduction, and business value realization.

**Governance, Standards, Compliance & Privacy**

 

* Define and enforce enterprise TDM standards, governance, and operating policies.
* Ensure compliance with privacy, security, and regulatory requirements related to test data usage, storage, movement, masking, and de-identification.
* Oversee implementation of compliance and privacy controls for non-production data usage.
* Establish standards for secure handling of production-like data in test environments.
* Partner with security, risk, privacy, and compliance stakeholders to maintain appropriate controls and audit readiness.
* Promote consistent governance for test data access, retention, refresh, lineage, and lifecycle management.

**Delivery Enablement & Stakeholder Partnership**

 

* Enable delivery teams through timely, compliant, and high-quality test data services that improve engineering throughput and release readiness.
* Partner with segment quality engineering leaders and application teams to understand demand patterns and align TDM support to delivery roadmaps.
* Coordinate across environments and shared services to reduce delays related to data setup, refresh, and availability.
* Influence engineering and quality practices that improve testability, environment readiness, and quality outcomes.
* Collaborate with enterprise enablement and platform teams to standardize capabilities and reduce duplication.

**Metrics, Governance & Continuous Improvement**

 

* Define and monitor KPIs related to test data availability, provisioning speed, automation adoption, compliance adherence, data quality, and operational efficiency.
* Use data and insights to identify risks, bottlenecks, and improvement opportunities across TDM services.
* Drive continuous improvement initiatives to reduce manual work, increase data reliability, and improve customer satisfaction.
* Provide clear reporting and operational transparency to senior leadership and stakeholders.
* Build maturity roadmaps for enterprise TDM capabilities and measure progress against defined outcomes.

**Use your skills to make an impact**
=====================================

**Required Qualifications**

 

* Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or any technology related degree or equivalent experience.
* **10+ years** of experience in quality engineering, test data management, data engineering, software engineering, or related technical disciplines.
* **5+ years** of leadership experience managing enterprise-scale technology teams, including managers and geographically distributed associates.
* Experience leading or scaling **test data management**, data engineering, or quality engineering functions in a large enterprise environment.
* Demonstrated success building and operating secure, scalable, and compliant test data solutions.
* Experience with key TDM capabilities such as data provisioning, masking, obfuscation, de-identification, synthetic data generation, and lifecycle management.
* Strong understanding of privacy, security, and compliance considerations for test data in regulated environments.
* Experience driving automation and process modernization across engineering or quality workflows.
* Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills, with the ability to influence across engineering, quality, data, and business organizations.
* Experience working in Agile and DevOps environments and supporting modern software delivery practices.

**Preferred Qualifications**

 

* Experience in healthcare, payer/insurance, or another highly regulated industry.
* Experience supporting enterprise quality engineering or platform enablement organizations.
* Familiarity with test data management platforms, masking tools, synthetic data solutions, and data quality tooling.
* Knowledge of cloud platforms, distributed systems, APIs, CI/CD pipelines, and enterprise engineering platforms.
* Experience applying AI or machine learning capabilities to test data, quality engineering, or operational optimization.
* Familiarity with data governance, data retention, and environment management practices in large-scale enterprises.

**Success in this Role**

In this role, success will be measured by:

* Improved speed, reliability, and scalability of enterprise test data provisioning and support.
* Increased adoption of secure, compliant, and reusable TDM solutions across segments and teams.
* Reduced delivery delays caused by test data availability, quality, or environment coordination issues.
* Strong compliance with privacy, security, masking, and de-identification requirements.
* Measurable advancement in AI-enabled and automation-first TDM capabilities.
* Improved stakeholder satisfaction across Quality Engineering, Engineering, Product, and Delivery teams.
* Strong associate engagement, capability growth, and retention across the TDM organization.

Work at Home Requirements: To ensure Home or Hybrid Home/Office employees’ ability to work effectively, the self-provided internet service of Home or Hybrid Home/Office employees must meet the following criteria: At minimum, a download speed of 25 Mbps and an upload speed of 10 Mbps is required; wireless, wired cable or DSL connection is suggested. In certain roles, the minimum recommended internet speed required by Humana may not be sufficient for business needs. Humana reserves the right to require associates to upgrade their internet service if necessary. Work from a dedicated space lacking ongoing interruptions to protect member PHI / HIPAA information. 
Travel: While this is a remote position, occasional travel to Humana's offices for training or meetings may be required.

**Scheduled Weekly Hours**

40

**Pay Range**

The compensation range below reflects a good faith estimate of starting base pay for full time (40 hours per week) employment at the time of posting. The pay range may be higher or lower based on geographic location and individual pay will vary based on demonstrated job related skills, knowledge, experience, education, certifications, etc. 
$156,600 - $215,400 per year 
This job is eligible for a bonus incentive plan. This incentive opportunity is based upon company and/or individual performance.

**Description of Benefits**

Humana, Inc. and its affiliated subsidiaries (collectively, “Humana”) offers competitive benefits that support whole-person well-being. Associate benefits are designed to encourage personal wellness and smart healthcare decisions for you and your family while also knowing your life extends outside of work. Among our benefits, Humana provides medical, dental and vision benefits, 401(k) retirement savings plan, time off (including paid time off, company and personal holidays, paid parental and caregiver leave), short-term and long-term disability, life insurance and many other opportunities.

**About us**
============

About Humana: Humana Inc. (NYSE: HUM) is a leading U.S. healthcare company. Through our Humana insurance services and our CenterWell healthcare services, we make it easier for the millions of people we serve to achieve their best health – delivering the care and service they need, when they need it. These efforts are leading to a better quality of life for people with Medicare and Medicaid, families, individuals, military service personnel, and communities at large. Learn more about what we offer at Humana.com and at CenterWell.com.

**Equal Opportunity Employer**

It is the policy of Humana not to discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment because of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, marital status, genetic information, disability or protected veteran status. It is also the policy of Humana to take affirmative action, in compliance with Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act and VEVRAA, to employ and to advance in employment individuals with disability or protected veteran status, and to base all employment decisions only on valid job requirements. This policy shall apply to all employment actions, including but not limited to recruitment, hiring, upgrading, promotion, transfer, demotion, layoff, recall, termination, rates of pay or other forms of compensation and selection for training, including apprenticeship, at all levels of employment.

role.description:
**CoffeeBeverage Manufacturing | St. Louis, MO** **Know quality. Know food safety. Know coffee? Let's talk.** Ronnoco Beverage Solutions is looking for an experienced Director of QualityFood Safety to lead quality, food safety, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement across our manufacturing and warehousing operations.This is an opportunity to take your quality experience beyond a single production floor. You'll help set the standards that protect our products, our customers, and the consistency consumers expect from every cup. **What You'll Lead** **CoffeeBeverage Quality**Oversee quality standards across coffee, tea, and beverage products, from specifications and testing to packaging, labeling, warehousing, and customer requirements. The role works with product evaluation that includes the taste and aroma of coffee, tea, and beverage products.**Food SafetyRegulatory Compliance**Lead programs and audits involving SQF, HACCP, GMP, FDA, Kosher, Organic, and applicable health department requirements, while strengthening consistent food safety and sanitation standards across operations.**Quality SystemsContinuous Improvement**Use quality data, performance trends, operating practices, and controls to identify opportunities for improvement and build stronger, more consistent quality systems across company locations.**CustomerProduct Quality**Own product specifications, quality alerts, customer complaints, corrective actions, and quality issues involving packaging, labeling, order picking, and hand-packing.**Product HoldsRework**Partner with the Green Bean buyer on product holds and rework while directing the disposition of overage and damaged product.**Quality LeadershipTraining**Work alongside operations and cross-functional teams to develop clear, practical quality processes. You'll also oversee employees performing laboratory and quality testing and help identify and deliver quality-related training. **What We're Looking For** **You may be a great fit if you bring:**

* Bachelor's degree in a related field
* 3–5 years of quality and regulatory experience in food manufacturing
* Experience supporting quality programs across multiple locations
* Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
* The ability to spot trends in data and turn findings into action
* Experience with Microsoft Dynamics/Great Plains or a similar ERP
* Strong attention to detail and the ability to work independently
* A proactive, solutions-oriented approach

**Not a Desk-Only Quality Role** **You'll be where the product is.**The position blends office-based leadership with hands-on time in production, warehouses, laboratories, and receiving areas, including environments associated with roasting and processing. Travel of up to 25% to company facilities, co-manufacturers, suppliers, and customer sites is expected. **Ready to Make Your Mark on Every Cup?**If you're a quality professional who understands the discipline behind great food and beverage manufacturing and you're ready to influence quality across multiple operations, we'd like to hear from you. **Bring your expertise. Raise the standard. Help us protect the quality behind every cup.**Apply today to join Ronnoco Beverage Solutions in St. Louis.

Plant Manager

**About Us:**

TreeHouse Foods is a leading manufacturer of private label packaged foods and beverages, operating a network of over 20 production facilities and several corporate offices across the United States and Canada. At TreeHouse Foods, our commitment to excellence extends beyond our products and revolves around our people. We are investing in talent and creating a performance-based culture where employees can do their best work and develop their careers, directly impacting our mission to make high quality, affordable food for our customers, communities, and families. We hope you will consider joining the team and being part of our future.

Named one of America’s Best Large Employers by Forbes Magazine, we are proud to live by a strong set of values and strive to "Engage and Delight – One Customer at a Time." Guided by our values— **Own It, Commit to Excellence, Be Agile, Speak Up, and Better Together.** We are a diverse team driven by integrity, accountability, and a commitment to exceptional results. We embrace change, prioritize continuous learning, and foster collaboration, transparency, and healthy debate. Together, we set each other up for success to achieve enterprise-wide goals.

**What You Gain:**

* Competitive compensation and benefits program with no waiting period – you’re eligible from your first day!
* 401(k) program with 5% employer match and 100% vesting as soon as you enroll.
* Comprehensive paid time off opportunities, including immediate access to four weeks of vacation, five sick days, parental leave and 11 company holidays (including two floating holidays).
* Leaders who are invested in supporting your accelerated career growth, plus paid training, tuition reimbursement and a robust educational platform – DevelopU – with more than 10,000 free courses to support you along the way.
* An inclusive working environment where you can build meaningful work relationships with a diverse group of professionals. Take advantage of opportunities to build on our team-oriented culture, such as joining one of our Employee Resource Groups.
* Access to our wellness and employee assistance programs.

**Job Description:**

***About the Role:***

 

We are seeking a Plant Manager for our Cambridge, MD, facility, a leading manufacturer of quality aseptic products. This role is responsible for providing overall leadership and accountability for plant operations with a strong focus on delivering results. In partnership with the site leadership team, the Plant Manager will drive employee engagement, safety, quality, customer service, continuous improvement, cost management, and production performance to meet or exceed business objectives. The successful candidate will identify and implement strategic opportunities to improve operational efficiency, safety, throughput, productivity, schedule attainment, cost reduction, and product quality while fostering a positive and high-performing work environment.

 

***You will add value to this role by performing various functions including, but not limited to:***

* Providing coaching and leadership to team members in the areas of employee engagement, safety, quality, customer service, continuous improvement, cost, and equipment reliability to elevate the team’s performance.
* Promoting a safety culture and ensuring adherence to all health and safety policies/protocols.
* Leading the development, execution, and monitoring of the operations strategy in line with the overall operational objectives to achieve safety, quality and performance improvement and ensure achievement of manufacturing goals.
* Leading the continuous improvement program to deliver opportunities in cost, quality, food safety and service.
* Utilizing available data including OEE, line speed target, and efficiency and process data to continuously improve productivity, uptime, and reliability.
* Coordinating manufacturing activities with all other functions of the organization and suppliers to obtain optimum production and utilization of human resources, machines, and equipment.
Contribute to the development and execution of strategic plant-wide initiatives. 

 

***Important Details:***

* This is a full-time, on-site role on first shift. Occasional flexibility is required to support alternate shifts.
The anticipated compensation for this position ranges from $154,700.00 - 232,100.00 USD annually. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, seniority, geographic location, performance, shift, travel requirements, sales or revenue-based metrics and business or organizational needs. For certain roles, the successful candidate may be eligible for annual discretionary merit compensation award, bonus and equity pay. 

 

***You’ll fit right in if you have:***

* High school diploma or equivalent is required; Bachelor's degree in manufacturing, industrial technology, or related field is preferred.
* Minimum of five years of leadership experience in a production or food manufacturing environment.
* Strong leadership and team management skills.
* Experience leading in a union environment is preferred.
* Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing Principles.
* Knowledge of safety regulations, quality control procedures, and inventory management.
* Excellent problem-solving, troubleshooting, and decision-making skills.
Proficient in Microsoft Office. 

**Your TreeHouse Foods Career is Just a Click Away!**

Click on the “Apply” button or go directly to www.treehousefoods.com/careers to let us know you’re ready to join our team!

*At TreeHouse Foods, we embrace diversity and inclusion for innovation and growth. We are committed to building inclusive teams and an equitable workplace for our employees to bring their true selves to work to help us “Engage and Delight – One Customer at a Time”.* *TreeHouse Foods is an Equal Opportunity Employer that prohibits discrimination or harassment of any type. All qualified applicants are considered for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity or expression, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. role.title: Plant Manager - Alaska Naturals Bellingham
role.description:
Overview:

Trident Seafoods is North America’s largest vertically integrated seafood company—partnering with fishermen, employees, and communities to responsibly harvest, process, and share wild Alaska seafood with the world. With deep roots in Alaska and operating across the globe, Trident is a privately held company headquartered in Seattle, committed to nourishing the world while upholding the highest standards for safety, sustainability, and excellence.

At Trident Seafoods, we work together for something bigger than ourselves. From nourishing the world with the best protein on earth to protecting our oceans, serving our fishermen, and supporting communities in Alaska and beyond, here, you’ll find a values-driven culture where your growth matters, your work has purpose and your contributions are recognized and appreciated—because at Trident, we believe meaningful work connects us all.

Responsibilities:

**Summary:**

The Plant Manager leads all operations for Trident Seafoods’ Alaska Naturals facility in Bellingham, Washington, which produces fish oil and related nutritional products. This role has overall accountability for safe, reliable, compliant, and cost-effective plant performance, including production, quality, maintenance, technical processes, people leadership, and financial results.

The Plant Manager provides hands-on leadership in a specialized manufacturing environment and works closely with a small, experienced technical team to maintain process control, resolve complex production issues, improve yield and throughput, and ensure products consistently meet customer and regulatory requirements. The role establishes priorities for the site, develops team capability, manages operational risk, and aligns plant execution with Global Supply Chain and broader business objectives.

**Essential Functions: (Responsibilities, Tasks, Supervisory Needs)**

* Leads daily operations for the Alaska Naturals facility, including production, technical processes, maintenance coordination, quality, safety, staffing, and site administration.
* Assumes accountability for plant financial performance, including budget development, cost control, labor and material utilization, yield, inventory, capital priorities, and achievement of operating targets.
* Sets the site’s operating strategy and translates business priorities into clear short- and long-term goals, production plans, technical priorities, and accountability measures.
* Builds and sustains a strong safety culture and ensures compliance with the Trident Safety Program and applicable environmental, occupational safety, and process-safety requirements.
* Ensures the facility operates in compliance with applicable food safety, product quality, environmental, labeling, and regulatory requirements for fish oil and nutritional-product manufacturing.
* Provides direction and support to a small technical team, effectively leveraging specialized expertise while maintaining clear ownership, disciplined decision-making, cross-training, and continuity of critical knowledge.
* Partners with quality, engineering, maintenance, procurement, planning, logistics, commercial, and other cross-functional teams to resolve issues and ensure the reliable flow of raw materials and finished products.
* Directs the production plan and adjusts labor, equipment, materials, scheduling, and technical resources to improve safety, quality, service, throughput, yield, uptime, and cost performance.
* Monitors plant performance through meaningful operating metrics, identifies root causes and emerging risks, and ensures corrective actions are completed and sustained.
* Manages and develops direct reports by setting clear expectations, assigning work, providing timely coaching and feedback, evaluating performance, supporting development, and making people decisions in partnership with HR.
* Represents Alaska Naturals in operating reviews and communicates site results, risks, resource needs, and recovery plans clearly to business and functional leaders.

*Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these essential functions.*

Trident Seafoods offers a comprehensive and quality benefits package. Full-time employees may be eligible for discretionary/performance-based incentives, medical, dental and vision insurance plans, optional HRA/HSA, telemedicine, employee assistance and wellness programs, long-term disability, basic life and AD&D, and 401(k) with a company match, paid time off, 10 paid holidays each year, and paid parental leave. For full-time employees, the initial paid time off benefit starts at 20 days per year, adjusted commensurate with relevant experience. Commuter and transit programs are also available.

 
Qualifications:

**Travel/On-Call Requirements:** Minimal travel, up to 10%.

**Required Qualifications: (Education, Years of Experience, Certifications)**

* A minimum of 8 years of progressively responsible experience in manufacturing, processing, or plant operations, including experience leading operations and technical or maintenance employees.
* A bachelor's degree in engineering, operations management, or a related field, or the equivalent combination of education and years of experience

**Preferred Education & Experiences:**

* Experience in seafood, fish oil, edible oils, rendering, nutritional ingredients, food processing, chemical processing, or another process-manufacturing environment.
* Experience leading a specialized facility with a lean organizational structure and a small technical team.
* Experience with process controls, separation or refining processes, bulk-liquid handling, utilities, preventive maintenance, and capital projects.
* Continuous improvement experience using Lean, Six Sigma, root-cause analysis, or comparable problem-solving methods.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities (KSAs):**

* Demonstrated accountability for plant budgets, operating costs, production performance, and delivery of measurable operational results.
* Experience operating within regulated safety, quality, and environmental systems.
* Strong working knowledge of plant operations, process manufacturing, equipment reliability, quality systems, and environmental, health, and safety practices.
* Ability to lead through technical experts by asking effective questions, clarifying decision rights, integrating specialized input, and maintaining accountability for site results.
* Strong financial and analytical capability, including the ability to interpret plant operating data, identify performance drivers, and make sound trade-off decisions.
* Proven ability to diagnose problems, establish priorities, manage risk, and drive corrective actions to completion.
* Practical, visible leadership style with the ability to build trust, establish clear standards, and develop a capable and accountable team.
* Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to work effectively with employees, leaders, customers, vendors, regulators, and cross-functional partners.
* Proficiency with Microsoft Office and applicable plant reporting, planning, and performance-management systems.
* Ability to adapt to changing production, supply, customer, and business needs in a specialized operating environment.

**Work environment:**

This role takes place in both an office and production setting. While performing the duties of this job, the employee may be exposed to wet and/or humid conditions and moving mechanical parts. The employee is frequently exposed to outside weather conditions. The employee is occasionally exposed to high, precarious places; fumes or airborne particles; toxic or caustic chemicals; extreme cold; risk of electrical shock and vibration. The noise level in the work environment is moderate to loud.

**Work Ability Requirements:**

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to stand, walk; use hands to finger, handle, or feel and reach with hands and arms. The employee is occasionally required to climb or balance.

Additional Information:

*This position is not eligible for immigration sponsorship, including F-1 STEM-OPT authorization.*

*Stay connected with Trident Seafoods online at* *www.tridentseafoods.com* *and follow us on* *Facebook**,* *X**,* *Instagram**,* *Pinterest**,* *YouTube* *or* *LinkedIn* 
 
*Trident Seafoods provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.* 
 
*Trident Seafoods and its subsidiaries have adopted a drug-free workplace policy. Working under the influence of Drugs or Alcohol is not permitted.* 
 
*Employment with Trident Seafoods is contingent upon the candidate maintaining valid immigration status and work authorization throughout employment, with or without immigration sponsorship by the company.*

role.title: Director of Operations
role.description:
The Director of Operations owns every operational outcome at Bold Reuse: sanitation, logistics, inventory, quality, safety, and operating cost, in every market we serve. You will build and run the wash hubs that wash, sort, inspect, and recirculate millions of reusable items, and you will stand up new facilities fast without sacrificing quality or unit economics. This is a hands-on, in-person role based at a Bold Reuse operations facility in Seattle, WA or Portland, OR, with occasional travel to our other markets. You report to the CEO and lead the managers who run our wash hubs.

### **About Bold Reuse**

Bold Reuse is a full-service reuse platform that eliminates single-use waste. We’ve already eliminated more than 8 million pounds of packaging from the landfill, and we’re just getting started! Our mission is to make the circular economy a reality for any business that wants to reduce its packaging waste.

### **Description**

**Director of Operations**
==========================

**About Bold Reuse**
====================

Bold Reuse is a full-service reuse platform that eliminates single-use waste. We have already kept more than 10 million packaging items out of landfill. We serve stadiums, campuses, arenas, and large events, and we are now scaling our operations footprint to new markets across the US.

 
 

**The Role**
------------

The Director of Operations owns every operational outcome at Bold Reuse: sanitation, logistics, inventory, quality, safety, and operating cost, in every market we serve. You will build and run the operations facilities that wash, sort, inspect, and recirculate millions of reusable items, and you will stand up new facilities fast without sacrificing quality or unit economics.

 
 

This is a hands-on, in-person role based at a Bold Reuse operations facility in Portland, OR, Seattle, WA, San Francisco or Los Angeles, CA with occasional travel to our other markets. You report to the CEO and lead the managers who run our wash hubs.

 
 

We are looking for someone who treats every process as improvable: fewer touches per item, lower cost per unit, higher throughput, and zero quality escapes. When something goes wrong in operations, you own the fix, the root cause, and the system that prevents it from happening again.

Our main product is our service. Stadiums, arenas, and event operators stake their guest experience, their sustainability commitments, and their brand on our service working every time. A late delivery, a short count, or a cleanliness issue is not an internal problem; it is a failure our client feels in front of tens of thousands of fans. This leader must make decisions with that client impact in front of mind, every day and at every site.

 
 

**What You Will Own**
---------------------

End-to-end operational ownership

* Own the full operating P&L for sanitation and logistics across all markets, including labor, consumables, equipment, and facilities.
* Own operational KPIs and report on them weekly: throughput, cost per item, touches per item, on-time and in-full delivery, client service-level adherence, client satisfaction, quality escapes, and safety incidents.
* Be the single accountable owner for operational problems. Lead root-cause analysis and put permanent corrective actions in place, not workarounds.
* Own service delivery for clients, including readiness, staffing, and post-event recovery.

Client success through operational excellence

* Treat client outcomes as the ultimate measure of operational performance. Our clients succeed only when our operations run flawlessly.
* Understand each major client's operating model, event calendar, and sustainability goals, and design service to support them.
* Define and meet service-level commitments for every account: delivery windows, inventory availability, cleanliness, and recovery rates.
* Partner closely with Customer Success and Sales on onboarding, event readiness, and account reviews, so operational capability and client promises stay aligned.
* Weigh client impact in every operational decision, from staffing and scheduling to process changes and cost reductions.
* When service falls short, own the client communication alongside Customer Success, deliver the fix fast, and follow up with a clear corrective plan.

Scaling physical operations facilities

* Plan, launch, and ramp new wash and logistics facilities in new markets, from site selection and layout through equipment install, hiring, training, and steady-state operation.
* Build a repeatable market-launch playbook so each new plant reaches target throughput and cost faster than the last.
* Run capacity planning across markets so that equipment, labor, and inventory stay ahead of contracted demand.
* Make build, buy, and partner decisions on equipment and facilities, with clear ROI cases.

Efficiency, touch reduction, and cost

* Map every process from pickup to recirculation and systematically remove touches, handoffs, and waste.
* Apply lean and continuous-improvement methods (for example, value-stream mapping, standard work, 5S, kaizen) to raise throughput and cut cost per item.
* Identify and implement automation in sorting, washing, drying, inspection, and packing where the ROI supports it.
* Partner with product and engineering to embed operational data into our Circular Intelligence System and use it to drive decisions.

Quality control and food safety

* Own the quality management system for sanitation, including written standards, inspection points, testing, documentation, and audit readiness.
* Ensure every item meets food-contact sanitation standards and applicable health department and client requirements.
* Track and drive down defects, rewash rates, and damaged or lost inventory.
* Lead customer-facing quality responses and corrective action plans when issues occur.

Supply chain and inventory

* Manage inventory of reusable serviceware across its full lifecycle: procurement, deployment, return, loss, and retirement.
* Manage suppliers of equipment, chemicals, and materials, ensuring supply keeps pace with rapid growth at the right cost.

People and leadership

* Hire, develop, and lead market managers, and through them, hourly operations teams.
* Set clear goals and standards while giving local teams autonomy to solve problems.
* Build a culture of safety, accountability, and continuous improvement.
* Identify and advance top performers ready for greater responsibility.
 

 

**What You Bring**
------------------

Required

* 7+ years of operations leadership in manufacturing, warehousing, distribution, commercial laundry, food processing, or similar high-volume physical operations, including 5+ years managing managers.
* A proven record of rapidly scaling physical operations: opening or expanding plants, warehouses, or processing facilities and ramping them to target throughput and cost on a tight timeline.
* Demonstrated results driving efficiency, with specific examples of reducing touches, labor hours, or cost per unit through process redesign, lean methods, or automation.
* Hands-on experience building and managing quality control programs, including standards, inspection, corrective action, and audits. Food-safety or sanitation experience strongly preferred.
* Experience running client-facing or service-level-driven operations, where operational performance directly determined customer outcomes and retention.
* Full P&L or cost-center ownership for an operation, with a track record of hitting budget.
* Strong analytical skills: you build ROI cases, run operations on data, and are comfortable with operational systems and dashboards.
* Clear, direct written and verbal communication with teams, executives, and enterprise clients.

Preferred

* Experience in a fast-growing startup or a multi-site rollout.
* Lean Six Sigma (Green Belt or higher) or equivalent continuous-improvement training.
* Experience with commercial dishwashing, sanitation equipment, or reverse logistics.
* Experience with HACCP, ServSafe, or health department compliance.
* Experience supporting large live events or venues.
 

 

**Our Values and Competency Expectations**
------------------------------------------

At Bold Reuse, how we work matters as much as what we do. The Director of Operations is expected to model these competencies, with Ownership as the defining one for this role.

* Ownership: Owns outcomes across every operational activity, not just effort. Recognizes that our clients' success depends on our operations and acts accordingly. Anticipates problems before they reach clients, makes decisions without waiting, and closes the loop on root causes. Holds self and team accountable to measurable results.
* Boldness: Challenges how work is done and brings solutions, not just problems. Takes smart risks, weighing impact on customers and the business.
* Intentionality: Prioritizes by impact and urgency. Makes thoughtful decisions aligned with values and business goals. Models reliability and professionalism.
* Leadership: Builds alignment across people and teams. Delegates and creates ownership in others. Addresses conflict directly to maintain trust and momentum.
* Collaborative: Works across functions, synthesizes input, and raises the quality of work through feedback.
* Adaptable: Adjusts to changing conditions while keeping rigor and follow-through. Helps others navigate change.
* Loving: Shows emotional intelligence in hard moments. Supports teammates' growth and well-being. Models resilience and a growth mindset.
 

 

**Compensation and Benefits**
-----------------------------

This position has a salary range of $110,000 to $120,000 per year. This range is a good-faith estimate; the final offer depends on qualifications and experience. The package also includes equity options, medical, dental, and vision insurance, paid holidays, and paid time off. We can only hire US-based candidates at this time.

 
 

**How to Apply**
----------------

Send your resume and a cover letter to [email protected]. In your cover letter, describe a process you developed that measurably cut touches or cost, and an example of a time your operation's performance made or broke a customer's success.

 

#### **Salary**

$110,000 - $120,000 per year
