Plant Manager – Level 3 Water Treatment PlantNorth Greene Utilities (NGU)Baileyton, Tennessee

North Greene Utilities is seeking a certified Level 3 Water Treatment Plant Manager to lead operations at our Level 3 water treatment production plant in Baileyton Tennessee. This is a key leadership role responsible for the full management of plant functions, regulatory compliance, and a small team of operators.

Position Overview

The Plant Manager oversees all day-to-day and long-term operations of NGU’s Level 3 water treatment plant. The position ensures continuous production of safe, high-quality water that meets or exceeds all Tennessee Department of Environment and Conservation (TDEC) and U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) standards and guidance. The manager supervises, mentors, and develops a team of three subordinates while maintaining efficient, safe, and compliant plant operations.

Key Responsibilities

* Manage all plant functions and treatment processes to meet TDEC and EPA regulatory requirements and policy guidance.• Supervise, mentor, and train three subordinates. Two subordinates are expected to achieve Level 1 certification by mid-2027.• Develop, implement, and manage shift schedules to ensure continuous, reliable plant coverage.• Ensure compliance with all federal and state safety regulations and NGU safety protocols.• Conduct lifecycle and operational management of treatment infrastructure, including maintenance planning and capital needs.• Participate in daily stand-up meetings with the NGU management team.• Assist with HR requirements for subordinates, including ensuring compliance with company policies.• Monitor the health and welfare of subordinates.• Conduct biannual performance counseling for subordinates.• Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability to evolving operational requirements and tasks as directed by the Operations Supervisor and General Manager.• Maintain accurate records, reporting, and documentation required for regulatory compliance and internal management.

Qualifications

* Current Tennessee Level 3 Water Treatment Operator certification (required).• Proven experience in water treatment plant operations, preferably in a leadership or supervisory role.• Strong knowledge of TDEC and EPA drinking water regulations, treatment processes, and compliance requirements.• Ability to supervise, train, and develop staff.• Valid driver’s license and ability to meet any additional job-related certifications or requirements (e.g., safety, drug and alcohol screening).• Excellent communication, organizational, and problem-solving skills.• Commitment to safety, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement.

Compensation and Benefits

NGU offers very competitive wages, an IRA, health insurance, and dental coverage. Additional details on pay and benefits will be discussed with qualified candidates.

How to Apply

**Essential Responsibilities:**

 
 

* Creates and advocates for developmental opportunities for others; builds collaborative, cross-functional relationships. Solicits and acts on performance feedback; works with leaders and employees to set goals and provide open feedback and coaching to drive performance improvement. Pursues professional growth; hires, trains, and develops talent for growth opportunities; strategically evaluates talent for succession planning; sets performance management guidelines and expectations across teams / units. Oversees implementation, adapts, and stays up to date with organizational change, challenges, feedback, best practices, processes, and industry trends; shares best practices within and across teams. Fosters open dialogue amongst team members, engages, motivates, and promotes collaboration within and across teams; motivates teams to meet business objectives. Delegates tasks and decisions as appropriate; provides appropriate support, guidance and scope; encourages development and consideration of options in decision making; fosters access to stakeholders.
* Manages designated units or teams by translating business plans into tactical action items; oversees the completion of work assignments and identifies opportunities for improvement; ensures all policies and procedures are followed; partners with key stakeholders and business leaders to ensure products and/or services meet requirements and expectations while aligning with departmental strategies. Aligns team efforts; builds accountability for and measuring progress in achieving results; assumes responsibility for decision making; fosters direct reports to resolve escalated issues as appropriate. Communicates goals and objectives; incorporates resources, costs, and forecasts into team and unit plans; ensures matrixed resources are fulfilling service or performance requirements across reporting lines. Removes obstacles that impact performance; identifies and addresses improvement opportunities; guides performance and develops contingency plans accordingly; influences teams and units to operate in alignment with operational and business objectives.
* Manages client care by: providing direction to ensure effective member/patient advocacy as well as implementing customer feedback and/or investigating and resolving member/patient complaints to optimize satisfaction and address care issues; aligning teams on high-quality member/patient care experience and service standards, developing and training teams on standards; and aligning teams on the importance of proper referral of members/patients and developing standards for sharing information with providers.
* Manages compliant services by: overseeing daily operations across team to ensure up-to-date compliance with organizational, state, and federal guidelines as well as regulatory policies, standards, and procedures, leading consultations with Compliance; and developing and updating processes to guide teams on written and electronic documentation, records, and reports according to department, federal, and state regulations.
* Establishes high quality counseling services by: setting guidelines and expectations for facilitating psychological/behavioral interventions; overseeing communication with patients, members, or families to ensure all team members consistently act with empathy and support when sharing results, discussing treatment plans, providing resources, and answering questions; and developing standards for assessing and treating urgent, high-risk clinical situations (e.g., crisis, suicidal), sharing across teams to guide appropriate interventions and prompt resolutions.
* Manages evaluations and diagnoses by: sharing guidelines and coaching teams on member/patient assessments and mental health evaluations, sharing best practices for providing diagnoses and evidence-based treatment plans and approaches for identified diagnoses (e.g., individual and group therapy).
* Drives program development and management by: planning and coordinating adjustments to current therapy programs and future program implementation (e.g., in-/out-patient psychotherapy, chemical dependency) or new programs to enhance quality and effectiveness of services; building new systems and processes for outcome management as well as overseeing the implementation of improvements to clinical treatment programs, designs, or protocols; and analyzing the productivity of large, complex therapy programs for providers and ensuring the optimal utilization of programs.

The Plant Manager is responsible for the management, planning, and coordination of all precast manufacturing operations to meet DVP business goals, while providing leadership to all plant and yard personnel.

* Track key performance metrics and hold direct reports accountable for results
* Ensure all production and yard operations meet DVP quality control standards
* Track and manage the inventory levels of finished goods
* Oversee and manage all incoming materials to ensure adequate inventory levels are met
* Continually collect and review data to reduce inefficiencies and waste
* Successfully hire, supervise, train, and retain production/yard staff
* Evaluate and review employee’s performance for the purpose of determining skill level and training needs
* Coach and mentor employees to allow for increased responsibilities and career advancement. Lead by example.
* Promote and maintain a clean work environment
* Recommend purchases of additional equipment for efficiency, cost reductions and/or quality improvements
* Successfully work with Quality Control/Project Management to meet customer demand and expectations
* Perform any other duties as assigned by the General Manager

**Supervisory Responsibilities:**

* Supervision of Plant Supervisors

**Required Skills/Abilities:**

* Work with computer as necessary (Microsoft Word, Excel)

**Physical Requirements:**

* Standing and walking for extended periods of time

role.title: Director, Commercial Operations and Asset Management
role.description:
**SUMMARY:** The Director, Commercial Operations & Asset Management provides leadership over the operational execution and ongoing asset management of Rhyze’s Commercial lending platform. This role is accountable for establishing scalable, controlled processes across transaction closing, funding, participation, servicing and portfolio administration, while actively overseeing the performance, credit quality and risk profile of the commercial real estate loan portfolio.

The Director leads portfolio surveillance, borrower and property performance monitoring, covenant compliance, annual review coordination, delinquency management and the operational execution of workout and loss mitigation strategies. The position works closely with the Managing Director, Commercial; Capital Markets; and Legal, and coordinates with lead lenders, borrowers, servicing partners and participating credit unions as appropriate.

The successful candidate combines commercial real estate credit and asset management expertise with operational discipline, sound judgment, strong communication skills and a focus on scalable execution.

**DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:**

**Commercial Portfolio & Asset Management**

· Lead portfolio surveillance and risk-based monitoring of commercial real estate loans, including payment performance, DSCR, net operating income, occupancy, rent rolls, leasing, borrower liquidity, maturities and concentration exposure.

· Oversee borrower and property financial reporting, covenant testing and compliance calendars; identify reporting deficiencies, covenant breaches, emerging risks and required follow-up.

· Coordinate annual and interim credit reviews, risk-rating assessments, watchlist management and action plans, with documented findings, ownership, deadlines and management escalation.

· Oversee collateral protection requirements, including insurance, property taxes, escrows, reserves, liens, property inspections, appraisals and other third-party assessments, in coordination with Servicing and Legal.

**Special Assets & Loss Mitigation**

· Identify and escalate delinquencies, maturity or covenant defaults and deteriorating credits; coordinate borrower outreach, collection strategies and remediation plans for criticized or classified assets.

· Evaluate requests for waivers, modifications, extensions, forbearances and other accommodations; develop supporting analysis and recommendations for authorized decision-makers.

· Coordinate workout and loss mitigation activities with Commercial leadership, Legal and external counsel, including enforcement, bankruptcy or foreclosure matters when applicable.

· Prepare required participant notices and approval packages; document borrower communications, decisions, conditions and deadlines, and monitor execution and performance under approved resolution plans.

**Commercial Operations & Servicing Oversight**

· Lead day-to-day Commercial operations with clear accountability, service standards, quality controls and escalation procedures across the loan lifecycle.

· Oversee transaction closing, funding, loan boarding and post-closing administration, including conditions, documentation, milestone tracking, data transfers and outstanding exceptions.

· Coordinate with internal teams, servicing partners and Capital Markets on participation administration, payment processing, reconciliations, escrows, reserves, borrower notices, payoffs, releases and related servicing matters.

· Ensure accurate implementation and recording of approved modifications, extensions and other post-closing actions, consistent with loan documents, participation agreements, delegated authority and applicable requirements.

**Operational Excellence, Reporting & Scalability**

· Provide timely loan-level and portfolio reporting to management and participating investors, including delinquencies, covenant exceptions, watchlist activity, material credit events and remediation progress.

· Serve as a central coordinator across Commercial, Capital Markets, Finance, Legal, servicing partners, lead lenders and participating credit unions on operational and portfolio matters.

· Develop and standardize procedures, controls, checklists, templates and reporting; identify opportunities for automation, integration and improved data quality to support scalable growth.

· Establish and monitor key performance indicators, including reporting compliance, review completion, exception aging, delinquency trends, watchlist resolution and transaction cycle times.

**Other**· Responsible for effective self/workload management. Demonstrates clear written and verbal communication skills. Promotes collaboration and a positive, professional work environment. Attends all position related meetings to ensure proper communication/planning occurs.

· Performs other related duties as assigned by the Managing Director

· Complies with all company policies, procedures, and regulatory requirements.

· Care for non-public information (NPI) and ensuring that confidentiality of company, borrowers, and partner information is maintained.

· Responsible for contributing to a positive work environment and culture that represents the company values.

**QUALIFICATIONS:**

· Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Administration, or a related field preferred; equivalent professional experience considered.

· Minimum of 10 years of progressive experience in commercial real estate lending, commercial credit administration, loan servicing, asset management, or a related field, with demonstrated experience managing commercial loan portfolios.

· Strong understanding of the end-to-end commercial lending lifecycle, including loan documentation, closing, funding, servicing, portfolio administration, and loan participations.

· Demonstrated expertise in commercial real estate asset management, including financial statement analysis, property performance monitoring, debt service coverage, covenant compliance, collateral valuation, and credit risk assessment.

· Experience identifying and managing problem loans, including delinquencies, covenant defaults, borrower accommodations, forbearances, modifications, workouts, and loss mitigation strategies.

· Strong knowledge of commercial loan servicing practices, including payment administration, escrow and reserve management, collateral protection, and post-closing compliance.

· Demonstrated ability to evaluate portfolio performance, identify emerging credit risks, develop actionable recommendations, and effectively communicate findings to management and other stakeholders.

· Experience establishing and improving operational processes, internal controls, reporting practices, and technology-enabled workflows to support efficiency, accuracy, and scalability.

· Strong understanding of commercial lending regulatory requirements, credit policies, risk management practices, and financial institution governance.

· Proven ability to manage multiple priorities, coordinate cross-functional activities, and lead complex initiatives with a high degree of accountability and attention to detail.

· Excellent analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills, with the ability to effectively engage borrowers, lending partners, credit union executives, and internal stakeholders.

· Self-motivated, adaptable, and comfortable operating independently in an entrepreneurial, growth-oriented environment.

Pay: $165,000.00 - $185,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* Dental insurance
* Flexible spending account
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Life insurance
* Paid time off
* Retirement plan
* Vision insurance

Work Location: Remote

role.title: Director of Operations – Medical Practice
role.description:
Medical Practice Administration | Muncie Primary Care

Full-Time | On-Site | Monday–Friday

Competitive annual salary, depending on experience and qualifications, with the opportunity for an additional performance-based bonus.

45 Years of Excellence. An Exciting Future Ahead.

Founded in 1981, Muncie Primary Care is a family-owned, independent primary care practice with deep roots in East Central Indiana.

For 45 years, we've built our reputation on exceptional patient care, strong community relationships, and a commitment to independent medicine. Today, the next generation of physician leadership is carrying that legacy forward.

With a newly renovated facility and continued investments in our people, technology, and patient experience, we're excited about what's ahead.

We're proud of what we've built. We're looking for someone who's excited to help us make it even better.

*This Isn't Your Typical Office Manager Position.*

We're looking for an experienced, forward-thinking Director of Operations who can serve as the second-in-command to our physician-owner and CEO, leading the day-to-day operations of our practice while helping us build a stronger, more efficient organization for the future.

This is a true leadership position focused on developing people, improving processes, strengthening accountability, overseeing financial and operational performance, and turning ideas into action.

**What You'll Do**

1. Lead Operations and Financial Performance

* Provide overall leadership and oversight of daily practice operations, ensuring that clinical and administrative departments work together efficiently.
* Identify operational challenges, develop practical solutions, and address issues proactively before they escalate.
* Oversee operational budgets, monitor expenses, review financial performance, and identify opportunities to improve efficiency and profitability.
* Work with designated team members responsible for administrative functions, technology, vendor coordination, and other business operations to ensure these responsibilities are managed effectively.
* Establish clear systems for delegation, communication, follow-through, and accountability.
* Ensure appropriate processes are in place for regulatory compliance, organizational policies, and operational risk management.

2. Lead, Develop, and Support Our Team

* Build and maintain strong, positive working relationships with employees across all departments.
* Develop departmental leaders, encourage professional growth, and help employees succeed in their roles.
* Foster a workplace culture built on mutual respect, open communication, teamwork, and accountability.
* Provide coaching, performance feedback, and support with difficult conversations and conflict resolution.
* Address employee concerns and interpersonal challenges fairly, promptly, and professionally.
* Work collaboratively with our Marketing/Human Resources Manager on recruitment, employee development, retention, and performance management.
* Strengthen communication and cooperation between clinical and administrative departments.

3. Improve Systems and Use Data to Drive Decisions

* Develop, monitor, and analyze Key Result Areas (KRAs), Key Performance Indicators (KPIs), scheduling utilization, productivity, and other operational performance measures.
* Identify inefficiencies, evaluate workflows, and implement improvements that enhance patient access, employee satisfaction, and practice performance.
* Build systems that promote consistency, clear responsibilities, effective delegation, and measurable accountability.
* Use spreadsheets, dashboards, financial information, and operational data to identify trends and guide decision-making.
* Evaluate the results of operational changes and make adjustments as needed.
* Help create an organization where problems are identified early and addressed effectively.

4. Help Shape the Future of Our Practice

* Partner directly with the physician-owner and CEO on strategic planning, organizational priorities, and practice improvement initiatives.
* Translate long-term goals into practical action plans, timelines, and measurable outcomes.
* Explore opportunities to leverage AI, automation, and emerging technology to reduce administrative burden and improve efficiency.
* Take ownership of projects from initial planning through implementation and evaluation.
* Anticipate challenges, identify opportunities, and bring forward thoughtful solutions and recommendations.
* Help balance the needs of patients, providers, employees, and the business while supporting the long-term success of independent primary care.

**You might be a great candidate for this position if….**

* You're a natural leader who enjoys developing people, building relationships, and helping teams succeed.
* You build trust and respect while maintaining clear expectations and accountability.
* You're proactive, resourceful, and comfortable making decisions, solving problems, and taking ownership of outcomes.
* You communicate effectively, navigate difficult conversations professionally, and foster collaboration across departments.
* You enjoy improving processes, building efficient systems, and finding better ways to get things done.
* You're comfortable using financial information, spreadsheets, and performance metrics to guide decisions.
* You're excited about new technology, including AI and automation, and enjoy working with an engaged owner who values initiative and independent thinking.

**This Position May Not Be the Right Fit If...**

* You prefer a traditional office management role focused on completing daily administrative tasks.
* You're most comfortable waiting for direction rather than taking ownership of challenges.
* You prefer maintaining existing processes rather than finding a better way to do things.
* You find it difficult to address employee performance concerns or navigate uncomfortable conversations.
* You tend to focus on identifying problems without taking responsibility for developing and implementing solutions.
* You aren't comfortable using data, financial information, or technology to evaluate performance and guide decisions.

We recognize that no candidate will bring every skill or have every answer on day one. We're looking for someone with the leadership ability, judgment, curiosity, and initiative to learn, adapt, and grow with our practice.

**Qualifications**

***Required***

* Demonstrated leadership and management experience, including supervising employees, developing teams, and overseeing complex operational workflows.
* Strong interpersonal and communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to build productive working relationships.
* Experience coaching employees, addressing performance concerns, resolving conflicts, and fostering an accountable, team-oriented workplace.
* Proven ability to identify operational problems, implement solutions, and follow projects through to completion.
* Experience managing business operations, delegating responsibilities, and coordinating work across departments.
* Strong organizational skills, sound judgment, initiative, and the ability to make independent decisions.
* Comfort with technology, willingness to learn new tools, and an interest in using data to improve operational performance.

**Strongly Preferred**

* A bachelor's degree in business administration, healthcare administration, management, or a related field.

**Why Muncie Primary Care?**

We're an established, family-owned practice that values our employees, our patients, and our independence. We're proud of our history and equally excited about our future.

As our Director of Operations, you'll have:

* The opportunity to shape the systems, culture, and future direction of an established practice.
* Competitive base salary
* Opportunity for an additional performance-based bonus.
* Monday–Friday work schedule.
* Health insurance.
* Paid time off and paid holidays.
* Retirement benefits, subject to plan eligibility.

**Ready to Help Us Take the Next Step Forward?**

We're not looking for someone who has all the answers.

We're looking for someone who asks great questions, builds strong relationships, takes initiative, enjoys solving problems, and is excited about building something meaningful.

If you're an experienced leader who loves developing people, improving systems, taking ownership, and helping an organization succeed, we'd love to hear from you.

Pay: From $80,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* 401(k)
* 401(k) matching
* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Health savings account
* Paid time off

Application Question(s):

* Leadership and Initiative: Tell us about a process, system, or operational improvement you personally led. What was the problem, what did you change, and what was the result?
* Difficult Conversations: Describe a time you had to address a difficult situation with an employee or colleague involving performance, accountability, or workplace behavior. How did you approach the conversation, and what was the outcome?
* Data and Decision-Making: Tell us about a time you used data, performance metrics, or other measurable information to identify a problem or make a decision. What did you learn, and what action did you take?

Location:

* Muncie, IN 47304 (Preferred)

Work Location: In person

role.title: Head of Aircraft Production (R6147)
role.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube. 


About Shield AI:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense technology company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Our products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. 
Job Description:
We’re looking for a hands-on manufacturing leader to take X-BAT from early prototype builds through production launch and into rate production. 
You will lead prototype build execution and the manufacturing setup of our new Seattle-area facility, X-Forge 3. You’ll build the production team, establish the factory’s operating system and deliver the readiness needed to scale aircraft production safely, reliably and efficiently. 
This role carries accountability across the full journey: turning lessons from development builds into a repeatable production system, then leading that operation against safety, quality, delivery and cost commitments. You’ll work closely with Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain and Program Management to make that happen. 

What you'll do:
Lead prototype builds and new product introduction
Own the day-to-day execution of X-BAT prototype and development aircraft builds, including assembly, integration, rework and build support for testing.
Partner with Program Management to establish achievable build schedules, resource plans and milestones, making constraints and trade-offs visible early.
Work with Engineering and Manufacturing Engineering through build-test-learn cycles, ensuring build issues are captured, resolved and reflected in future designs and production processes.
Plan and execute pre-series builds to prove tooling, work instructions, material flow, process controls and workforce readiness before production ramp.
Maintain configuration discipline and aircraft traceability throughout development builds in partnership with Engineering and Quality.
Establish the Seattle production operation
Lead manufacturing setup and operational readiness for X-Forge 3, working with Facilities and Manufacturing Engineering on factory layout, equipment installation, commissioning and production flow.
Recruit, develop and lead the production organization, building capable frontline leadership and a skilled aircraft assembly team.
Own production staffing, training and capacity plans, aligning investment and workforce growth with program demand.
Drive launch readiness across people, tooling, materials, processes and quality, with clear owners and closure plans for gaps.
Lead the transition from prototype operations into Seattle production, ensuring build knowledge and lessons learned transfer with the work.
Deliver and scale aircraft production
Own production execution against safety, quality, delivery and cost targets as X-BAT moves through initial production and into sustained rate.
Establish daily operating routines, visual management and escalation processes that surface problems early and drive timely resolution.
Improve throughput, labor productivity, first-pass quality and schedule adherence through practical Lean methods and structured problem-solving.
Partner with Supply Chain and Planning to align material availability, supplier readiness and outsourced manufacturing with the production plan.
Work with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality to eliminate recurring build issues and embed permanent corrective actions.
Deploy digital manufacturing tools and appropriate automation to improve execution, traceability and scalability.
Give leadership a clear view of production performance, launch readiness, risks and the decisions needed to maintain progress.
Required qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, manufacturing or a related technical field.
10+ years of experience in aerospace or comparable advanced manufacturing, including at least 5 years leading production teams.
Demonstrated experience leading prototype or new product introduction builds and carrying a product into sustained production.
Proven ability to build and scale manufacturing operations, including workforce development, capacity planning and production systems.
Experience leading complex assembly and integration operations with demanding quality, configuration and traceability requirements.
Strong understanding of manufacturing readiness, tooling validation, material coordination and production launch.
Track record of improving safety, quality, delivery and cost through Lean manufacturing and structured problem-solving.
Ability to lead across Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain and Program Management, resolving competing priorities and driving clear accountability.
A hands-on leadership style, with the ability to move between long-term factory planning and detailed problem-solving on the floor.
Preferred qualifications:
Direct experience taking a new aircraft program from prototype through initial and rate production.
Experience establishing a new manufacturing facility or transferring production between sites.
Experience in aircraft final assembly, systems integration and production test.
Familiarity with aerospace quality systems, including AS9100, and digital manufacturing and traceability tools.
Experience managing production interfaces with outsourced manufacturing partners and complex supplier networks.
Advanced degree or relevant training in manufacturing leadership, program management or production launch.

role.title: Director, Operations Program Management
role.description:
Agility’s commercially deployed humanoids operate alongside teams in warehouses, manufacturing facilities, and distribution centers—tackling physically demanding and repetitive tasks while enabling workers to focus on higher-value work. With industry-leading safety standards and years of proven deployment data, we're pioneering a new era of automation that enhances human potential.

 About the Role 

 Agility Robotics is scaling its operations — and the programs that enable that scale need to be led with rigor, depth, and autonomy. As Director, Operations Program Management, you will own two things simultaneously: a team of technical and non-technical program managers working across all of the operations and supply chain domains and a portfolio of high-complexity programs that span the full organization. 

 Reporting to the Sr. Director of Operations Program Management & Insights, you will bring the structure, judgment, and leadership presence to operate with minimal oversight. You set the standard for what great program management looks like on this team. 

 This is the right role for someone who leads from the front, develops the people around them, and can drive complex cross-functional programs to outcomes without being told how to get there. 

 About the Work 

 
 Lead and develop a team of dedicated program managers. Set clear expectations, coach toward growth, and hold yourself accountable to building a stronger team over time. 

 Establish and model PM best practices across the team. You are both the standard-setter and the coach. 

 Own, through your and the team’s efforts, a portfolio of complex programs that require a high degree of structure, judgment, and organizational reach. Act as a player-coach on the team’s broader portfolio — holding your own programs while helping your direct reports navigate blockers and deliver against theirs. 

 Translate complex, multi-org work into clear progress narratives for executive audiences. You know what leadership needs to see and how to present it. 

 Identify risks, stalled decisions, and at-risk dependencies before they become problems.  

 Other duties as assigned. 

 
 About You 

 
 10+ years in leadership roles, with a proven track record in Program Management. 

 Exceptional ability to translate complex concepts into clear messages for diverse audiences. 

 Build and mentor a diverse and growing team of technical and non-technical Program Managers. 

 Strong data-driven decision-making skills to manage a complex portfolio of initiatives across a range of departments. 

 Operate with a high degree of autonomy defining the path for you and the team. 

 Deep understanding of how manufacturing and operations environments work — with 7+ years of experience driving programs in this space. 

 Comfort working in organizations without mature systems, clean data, or clear processes. 

 
 Bonus Points 

 
 Prior experience managing or developing a team of program managers. 

 Background in high-growth hardware, automation, or robotics environments. 

 Experience designing or overhauling operational processes at scale — service operations, order fulfillment, or manufacturing workflows. 

 
 
  

 Location 

 
 This is a hybrid position based out of our Salem office.

 
 The final salary offered to a successful candidate will be dependent on several factors that may include but are not limited to: job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Agility Robotics is a multi-state employer and this salary range may not reflect positions who work in other locations. These ranges may be modified in the future. 
 Anticipated Base Salary Range
 $149,000 — $193,000 USD 


 In addition to base pay, our competitive total rewards package consists of the following for full-time employees: 

 
 401(k) Plan:   Includes a 6% company match.

 Equity:   Company stock options.

 Insurance Coverage:   100% company-paid medical, dental, vision, and short/long-term disability insurance for employees.

 Benefit Start Date:   Eligible for benefits on your first day of employment.

 Well-Being Support:   Employee Assistance Program (EAP).

 Time Off: 
 
 Exempt Employees:   Flexible, unlimited PTO and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown.

 Non-Exempt Employees:   10 vacation days, paid sick leave, and 12 company holidays, including a winter shutdown, annually.

 


 On-Site Perks:   Catered lunches four times a week and a variety of healthy snacks and refreshments at our Salem and Pittsburgh locations.

 Parental Leave:   Generous paid parental leave programs.

 Work Environment:   A culture that supports flexible work arrangements.

 Growth Opportunities:   Professional development and tuition reimbursement programs.

 Relocation Assistance:   Provided for eligible roles.

 Annual Discretionary Bonus: Provided for eligible roles.

 
 All of our roles are U.S.-based. Applicants must have current authorization to work in the United States. 

 Agility Robotics is committed to a work environment in which all individuals are treated with respect and dignity. Each individual has the right to work in a professional atmosphere that promotes equal employment opportunities and prohibits unlawful discriminatory practices, including harassment. Therefore, it is the policy of Agility Robotics to ensure equal employment opportunity without discrimination or harassment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital status, citizenship, national origin, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law. Agility Robotics prohibits any such discrimination or harassment. 

  

 Agility Robotics does not accept unsolicited referrals from third-party recruiting agencies.  We prioritize direct applicants and encourage all qualified candidates to apply directly through our careers page.  If you are represented by a third party, your application may not be considered.  To ensure full consideration, please apply directly.

Ursa Major was founded to revolutionize how America and its allies access and apply high-performance propulsion, from hypersonics to solid rocket motors, satellite maneuvering and launch. We design and deliver propulsion and defense systems that solve the most urgent and critical national security demands.  

 Overview :
Ursa is seeking a strong production leader who can lead and build a team to scale production with a focus on safety and best-in-class industrial engineering principles. Ursa has developed a novel manufacturing method that can surge production levels across various products, employing mixed model strategy and early design for manufacturability. This position will heavily influence the standardization and scaling of these production lines. role.title: Head of Bedrock Operations Center
role.description:
JOIN THE TEAM BRINGING AUTONOMY TO THE BUILT WORLD


At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.

In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.

This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a Head of Bedrock Operations Center (BOC) to build and lead the central, always-on hub that oversees our deployed autonomous machines. As the Bedrock System deployments scale across new states, new machine types, and a next-generation platform, the BOC is how we keep every machine safe, productive, and supported around the clock.

This role owns three core functions: Remote Assistance, supporting autonomous machines in real time when they need a human decision; Customer & Partner Support, the single front door for customers, partners, and field teams; and Central Operations, which provides live visibility, dispatch coordination, and incident coordination and command.

The Head of BOC owns the Operations Center's operating model, organization, tooling requirements, performance, and manpower oversight. The BOC is accountable for the safe remote operations, uptime, and responsiveness our customers experience. Reporting to the VP of Operations, this leader is a critical thought partner to Product and to Operations Leads across the company.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

Operations Center Strategy & Build-out

 - Define the BOC operating model, org structure, and coverage model (shifts, time zones, follow-the-sun) as the fleet scales

 - Build and lead the BOC leadership team and a growing workforce of shift leads and specialists

 - Own workforce planning and ensure adequate, qualified staffing; Partner with Product and Engineering on machines-per-operator ratios against fleet growth, product mix, and new machine types

 - Own the physical and technical readiness of the Operations Center, including infrastructure, redundancy, connectivity, and business continuity

Remote Assistance

 - Own round-the-clock remote operations for autonomous machines, including response-time SLAs, escalation protocols, and clear decision authority

 - Establish safety-first standards for remote interventions, remote stops, and hand-offs to on-site personnel, in partnership with Safety teams

 - Build training, certification, and quality-assurance programs for remote assistance operators

 - Analyze intervention data and partner with Autonomy Engineering to reduce interventions and improve machine autonomy over time

Customer & Partner Support

 - Build and lead a tiered support function (L1 / L2 / L3) with clear escalation paths into Field Operations, Service, Hardware, RA, and/ or Engineering

 - Define and deliver support SLAs tailored to each product line and customer commitment

 - Own ticketing, knowledge base, and customer communication standards; turn voice-of-customer trends into fixes

 - Partner with the Commercial team on customer onboarding, service commitments, and account health

Central Operations / Command & Control

 - Own live, fleet-wide situational awareness: machine status, health, location, and utilization across every site

 - Coordinate daily dispatch, service, and maintenance with Field Operations, including parts and technician routing

 - Serve as incident command for operational and safety events, with clear playbooks for triage, escalation, communication, and post-incident review

 - Own runbooks, shift hand-off standards, and change management for new sites, new machine types, and new platforms

Performance & Analytics

 - Define and track core BOC metrics: intervention rate and response time, resolution time, SLA attainment, fleet uptime, customer satisfaction, and cost to serve

 - Run operational review cadences that drive accountability and bring key insights to leadership

 - Lead continuous improvement through process, automation, and data, increasing the number of machines each operator can safely support


WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Autonomous machines get fast, safe human support whenever they need it

 - Customers and partners have one clear front door and consistently fast resolution

 - Real-time visibility into every machine and site, with incidents handled calmly and transparently

 - Machines-per-operator rises steadily as intervention insights drive autonomy improvements

 - The Operations Center scales ahead of fleet growth, new sites, and new machine types without a drop in service


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required

 - 12+ years in operations leadership, including 5+ years building and leading 24/7 or mission-critical operations (command centers, remote operations, network or fleet operations, or large-scale support organizations)

 - Experience building an operations organization from early stage to scale, including hiring and developing managers and shift leads and managing large hourly and/or contract workforces

 - Track record defining and managing SLAs, escalation paths, and incident response in safety-critical or high-availability environments

 - Experience influencing engineering, product, and commercial leaders, driving difficult decisions, and managing risk through rapid growth

 - Strong analytical skills; comfortable with operational data, dashboards, and forecasting models (SQL / BI tools a plus)

 - Experience with workforce planning, scheduling, and shift-based operations

 - Excellent written and verbal communication with customers, field crews, and executives

Preferred

 - Experience running operations centers for autonomous vehicles, robotics, trucking, aviation, or mining

 - Experience leading remote assistance, teleoperation, or fleet response teams for autonomous systems

 - Familiarity with heavy machinery and/or the construction industry

 - Experience building B2B or technical support for industrial equipment or hardware products

 - Familiarity with fleet telemetry, monitoring and alerting, ticketing, and workforce-management tools

 - Experience launching operations across multiple regions or time zones

 - Continuous improvement / Lean / Six Sigma experience


WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

Every autonomous machine Bedrock deploys depends on the Operations Center to keep it safe, productive, and supported. You'll build the function that lets our fleet scale with confidence, and directly shape the experience every customer and partner has with Bedrock.

Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer

We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.

Reasonable Accommodations

We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please let your recruiter know so we can support you.

role.title: Director, Supplier Industrialization Engineering
role.description:
At Relativity Space, we’re building rockets to serve today’s needs and tomorrow’s breakthroughs. Our Terran R vehicle will deliver customer payloads to orbit, meeting the growing demand for launch capacity. But that’s just the start. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond the known. 

 Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us. 

 About the Team:  

 The Reliability team at Relativity Space ensures quality is built into every stage of the Terran R design and production process, embedding reliability from the very beginning. The team works directly with design, manufacturing, test, and launch teams to stay close to the hardware, understand constraints, and proactively shape decisions. As the program moves from development into production and scaled operations, this is the time to establish the right processes, controls, and inspections without slowing progress. The team plays a key role in balancing risk, fostering a culture of ownership, and making sure speed never comes at the cost of reliability. Success means creating a quality system that scales with the Terran R program and Relativity as a whole. 

 About the Role: 

 
 Develop and lead a high-performing Supplier Development Engineering team, fostering ownership, technical rigor, and data-driven decision-making. 

 Set and execute the supplier development strategy, reliability roadmap, and SQMS processes to meet Terran R production, launch, and compliance requirements (AS9100/ISO 9001). 

 Drive supplier performance management, establishing key metrics and scorecards to improve PPM, yield, PPAP timing, and overall supplier capability. 

 Own major supplier risk escalation and resolution, guiding disciplined problem solving (e.g., 8D) and ensuring rapid recovery on quality or capacity issues. 

 Lead cross-functional alignment with Engineering, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain on supplier qualification, technical requirements, and NPI execution. 

 Oversee technical and operational execution, including supplier qualification, APQP/DFM/DFA, PPAP/FAIR approvals, and CI initiatives (Lean/Six Sigma) to ensure robust manufacturing and protect build schedules.   

 
 About You: 

 
 Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Aerospace, Industrial, or a related technical field) 

 10+ years of experience in Supplier Industrialization, Supplier Development, or Manufacturing Engineering, ideally within the aerospace or a high-reliability/safety-critical industry. 

 5+ years of direct people management experience, including coaching, mentorship, and performance management of an engineering team 

 Expert knowledge of quality systems (AS9100/ISO 9001) and core quality tools (APQP, PPAP, FAIRs, PFMEA, Control Plans), with a proven ability to influence the implementation and compliance of key quality initiatives. 

 Demonstrated capability to build processes from the ground up and successfully deploy them across diverse teams. 

 Willingness to travel up to 50% of the work week when needed.   

 
 Nice to haves but not required:    

 
 Master’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Aerospace, Industrial, or a related technical field). 

 Professional certification such as Six Sigma Black Belt, ASQ Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), or PMP. 

 Familiarity with high-volume inspection methods and data-driven acceptance methods. 

 Strong knowledge of enterprise applications (i.e., PLM, ERP, MES) and proficient in data analysis.   

 At Relativity Space, we are committed to transparency and fairness in our compensation practices. Actual compensation will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and other job-related factors. 

 Compensation is only one part of our total rewards package. Relativity Space offers competitive salary and equity, a generous PTO and sick leave policy, parental leave, an annual learning and development stipend, and more! To see some of the benefits & perks we offer, please visit here. 

 Hiring Range:
 $195,000 — $293,000 USD 


 We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status. 

 If you need a reasonable accommodation, please contact us at accommodations@relativityspace.com . 

 Please note: Relativity Space does not accept unsolicited resumes, candidate profiles, or referrals from recruitment agencies or search firms. Any unsolicited submission - via email, our website, social media, or directly to an employee - will be deemed the property of Relativity Space, and no fee will be owed absent a current, fully executed agreement with Talent Acquisition that specifically authorizes submissions for the applicable role.

role.title: Director of Manufacturing
role.description:
ABOUT FLUIDSTACK

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it. 


We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!




HOW WE OPERATE

 - Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

 - Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

 - Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

 - Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

 - Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.




THE MANUFACTURING TEAM

The Manufacturing team builds and scales Fluidstack's production system for gigawatt-scale infrastructure.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

 - Scale a manufacturing engine that outgrows the industry's pace. Grow capacity and capability across the full production process, so the team can take on more products and higher volume faster than anyone else builds.

 - Build the ecosystem behind gigawatt-scale infrastructure. Build and operate the full manufacturing ecosystem, not just a line, so output compounds as fast as the company scales.

 - Be the engine that grows faster than the company itself. Solve problems faster, think bigger, and develop yourself and your team as dynamically as Fluidstack scales around you.


ROLE SCOPE

 - Manage the plant bench. Manage a bench of plant managers across multiple manufacturing sites, setting the production, quality, and safety bar every plant is held to.

 - Own plant logistics. Own plant logistics end to end, inbound materials, in-plant flow, and outbound shipping, so schedule and cost never turn on a supply gap.

 - Keep plants running as designed. Work across Manufacturing Engineering and Supply Chain to keep every plant running as designed, catching gaps before they show up in output.

 - Hold the fleet to target. Set and hold production targets across the fleet, catching a struggling site early enough to fix it before it slips the build calendar.

 - Build the org. Build the manufacturing organization under you, hiring and developing plant managers as fast as new sites come online.


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would. https://jobs.ashbyhq.com/fluidstack/05c2e69c-42f9-4fcb-9cf0-a467aaf98f1c

 - You've managed multiple plant managers or site leaders at once, holding each to the same production and quality bar.

 - You've owned plant logistics, inbound materials, in-plant flow, and outbound shipping, not just the production line itself.

 - You've worked cross-functionally with manufacturing engineering, supply chain, and program teams to keep multiple plants running as intended.

 - You've caught a struggling site early and fixed it before it slipped a build or shipment schedule.

 - You write clearly enough to turn a fleet-wide production issue into a decision a CEO or COO can make in one read.

 - Bonus: Multi-site manufacturing operations (semiconductor, EV, battery, or industrial equipment). Supply chain and logistics network design. Lean or Six Sigma programs run at scale. P&L ownership across multiple facilities.


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

 - Work in non-climate-controlled environments, including active construction areas, data halls, electrical and mechanical rooms, and outdoor spaces. Temperatures can be high or low, and conditions can be humid, loud or dusty.

 - Lift, carry, push and pull up to 40 pounds on your own.

 - Sit, stand, walk, kneel, bend and crouch for long periods, including full shifts on your feet.

 - Wear the required personal protective equipment (PPE), such as hard hats, safety glasses, steel-toed boots, gloves and hearing protection, and follow site safety rules.

 - Climb stairs and ladders, and move around equipment, cable trays and uneven surfaces.



We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

AI Screening Notice https://fluidstack.io/legal/ai-screening-notice
Ashby Bias Audit https://fluidstack.io/legal/ashby-bias-audit

If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

role.title: Deputy Head of Production, Connected Warfare
role.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE SITE 

Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1 , its first hyperscale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed that autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America’s defense industrial base, strengthening America’s warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.



 ABOUT THE TEAM

 The Connected Warfare will set the standard for building the future at Arsenal-1 , our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ashville, OH. This team will have the opportunity to train under our world-class manufacturing team at Anduril HQ in Costa Mesa, CA for 3 months before bringing that standard of excellence back to Ohio.

 ABOUT THE ROLE 

As the Connected Warfare Deputy Head of Production, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of defense manufacturing by directly influencing the production of Anduril’s Connected Warfare product line. You will own the short-to-mid-term strategic development and execution of manufacturing operations, driving products to full-rate production. This role requires a dynamic leader who can serve as both a strategic architect and a hands-on executor, leading cross-functional teams to meet aggressive timelines and deliver products of the highest quality for our customers. You will contribute significantly to Anduril's vision of becoming a next-generation aerospace and defense manufacturer.

 What You'll Do: 

 
 Production Ownership & Strategy: Own all production outcomes for the Connected Warfare product line, including ramp plans, headcount, and the standing up of new manufacturing lines. Develop and execute a long-term strategy to rapidly scale production volumes to full-rate production.

 Leadership & Team Management: Serve as a strategic leader and tactical do-er, driving all people and resources across production to achieve outcomes. Lead cross-functional teams (including Production, Supply Chain, Quality, and Manufacturing Engineering) through strong leadership, advocacy, and a consistent on-site presence, holding them accountable to meeting demands, deadlines, and goals.

 Operational Excellence: Drive processes and systems needed throughout the product development lifecycle to mature products to full-rate production. Establish and manage the team to key performance indicators (KPIs) for financial, quality, and on-time delivery to optimize manufacturing operations' impact on the business.

 Quality & Compliance: Be accountable to AS9100D guidelines and drive a "quality-first" culture across all manufacturing operations.

 Process & Technology Advancement: Advise on development and oversee the implementation of digital technologies, from PLM and ERP to our custom MES and QMS systems, that enable our production operations to efficiently scale while meeting customer requirements. Shape corporate tools and processes to support the unique needs of aerospace production.

 
 Required Qualifications: 

 
 8+ years of proven experience overseeing the production and test of complex electromechanical products.

 Strong leadership experience managing large (100+ person) manufacturing teams and directing large cross-functional teams across planning, supply chain, manufacturing engineering, quality, and production to deliver products of the highest quality.

 A strong background in quality assurance, with a track record of driving a "quality-first" culture in a production environment and accountability to standards like AS9100D.

 Past success operating in both low-rate prototype and high-rate manufacturing environments, with a proven ability to scale production.

 High ownership and the ability to effectively manage multiple large projects and priorities in parallel, at a rapid pace, and report out on progress regularly.

 Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.

 Ability to work onsite five days a week at our Asheville, OH campus (Arsenal 1).

 
 Preferred Qualifications: 

 
 Success scaling production operations in a high-complexity manufacturing environment.

 Deep experience with the niche supply chains for aerospace and robotics.

 Demonstrated experience implementing and leveraging digital manufacturing technologies (PLM, ERP, MES, QMS) to drive efficiency and scale.

 Knowledge of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools.

role.title: Head of Production, Imaging
role.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE TEAM 

The Imaging Business Line, within Mission Systems Division, is responsible for tackling the most difficult problems involving computer vision, perception, electro-optical, infrared, and sensor data. The team develops state-of-the-art imaging systems across both hardware and software. Imaging products are deployed to tackle the most significant security challenges of America and its allies. The Imaging team is based in Lexington, Massachusetts.

We are seeking a Senior Director to coordinate all of our production operations across a variety of objectives and locations. The Head of Production owns execution, operational direction, career pathing, and production vision for a suite of Anduril products. Your job will be to provide consistent, flawless execution for a variety of products and programs.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO: 

 
 Own all Production outcomes such as, ramp plan, Headcount, etc.

 Drive all people and resources to drive all production outcomes.

 Serve as tactical leader for Anduril’s rapidly growing production operations for a product or suite of products.

 Hold cross functional teams accountable to meeting demands, deadlines and goals to deliver the production on time and within budget.

 Drive Production, Supply Chain, and Quality, teams to build and execute upon Anduril’s 5-year strategic vision to become a next-generation aerospace and defense manufacturer, capable of full rate production.

 Deliver production outcomes as the products mature from production development to full rate production.

 Build strong partnerships with Engineering, Deployment Operations, and Program Management to execute success.

 Mature products from low rate to full rate production by driving processes and systems as needed throughout the product development lifecycle.

 Establish and manage team to financial, quality, and on-time delivery KPIs to understand how our manufacturing operations are impacting our business.

 Advise on development and oversee implementation of digital technologies, from PLM and ERP to our custom MES and QMS systems, that enable our production operations to efficiently scale while meeting customer requirements.

 Be accountable to AS9100D guidelines.

 Be a partner to Anduril Imaging leadership for Manufacturing strategy.

 
 
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

 
 10+  years in a Production leadership role with a track record of successfully scaling products from prototype to full rate production on the order of 1000s.

 Strong ability to work cross-functionally in an unstructured, ambiguous environment. Startup experience preferred.

 Experience with discrete production operations in a deeply technical industry such as aerospace, consumer electronics, medical, or automotive. Production engineering  manufacturing experience also a plus.

 Must have owned a new product ramp through full rate production.

 Experience managing a P&L in a Production environment.

 Experience managing workforce of at least 100+ employees across quality, supply chain, manufacturing engineering and technicians.

 Relentless drive for continuous improvement and solving high impact business problems through highly leveraged process, business systems, and data.

 Strong outcome orientation with the ability to drive initiatives from inception to implementation and adoption. Willing and able to dive into tactical execution mode to move the effort forward.

 Ability to work with a strong engineering team on a technical level.

 Positive and inspirational leader with the demonstrated ability to assess, attract and retain high-quality talent and build high-performing teams.

 Strong problem solving and analytic skills with the ability to understand how problems and their solutions fit with the wider organization and its operations.

 Bachelor of Science or higher degree in a technical discipline preferred, not required.

 Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

 
  
 US Salary Range
 $261,000 — $346,000 USD 


 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:   

  

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

  

 
 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.



 
 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

 
 
 No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.



 Please always verify communications: 
 
 Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

 Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

 


 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.



 
 What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.



 


  

 Data Privacy 

 To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ .   

  

 By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

The team is developing deployable static and moving surface, undersea and sea to air vehicles, and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.



 ABOUT THE JOB

 We are seeking a Head of Production to join our team in Santa Ana, CA to stand up a cutting-edge manufacturing site. This role is crucial in ensuring that each initiative aligns with the company's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's success. You will build and lead the product line organization from scratch, establishing and managing manufacturing processes, quality systems, and the infrastructure needed to scale from prototype builds through full-rate production.

 As a leader in the Maritime Division, you must bear the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. Your spectrum of support will be exceptionally diverse and require you to rapidly drive aggressive deliverables to completion.

 The ideal candidate will leverage a deep expertise in large-scale manufacturing of a number of large, complex assemblies. You need to have experience in heavy fabrication, be able to lead the complex integration of different structures, and have a background spanning structural fabrication, joining and assembly across a variety of metals, alloys, and exotic materials. You need to have led an organization of hundreds, not dozens, and come from an operation comparable to the scale we are building at Anduril. You are a builder, not a caretaker.



 WHAT YOU’LL DO

 
 Own all production activity: manufacturing and production support.

 Build and lead the production organization, supporting hiring across manufacturing engineering, quality, and operations.

 Establish manufacturing processes and production infrastructure for complex electromechanical vehicles.

 Drive NPI and the manufacturing development lifecycle: Concept, Prototype, LRIP, FRP.

 Manage production budgets, schedules, and on-time delivery performance.

 Own production readiness reviews and design from the production system including production engineering.

 Coordinate with supply chain including demand planning, procurement, and warehouse operations.

 Implement and optimize production systems (ERP, MES, QMS).

 Drive continuous improvement using Lean, Six Sigma, or equivalent methodologies.

 Ensure compliance with AS9100, NAVSEA, and customer quality requirements.

 Interface with engineering, program management, and customer organizations.

 Travel over 75% to manufacturing facilities and customer sites.

 
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, or equivalent.

 Minimum 10+ years of experience in manufacturing or production for complex electromechanical systems.

 Minimum 5+ years of experience building and leading production teams and organizations.

 Experience managing production budgets in the $10M+ range.

 Demonstrated experience scaling production from NPI through full-rate production.

 Deep expertise with production systems (ERP, MES, QMS).

 Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

 
 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 
 Direct experience in maritime, naval, or aerospace defense, with knowledge of NAVSEA or MIL-SPEC standards.

 Technical foundation in mechanical assembly, electrical integration, heavy metal or composite fabrication, or shipbuilding or large vehicle production.

 Hands-on technical credibility having personally built, debugged, or repaired hardware in a production environment, and is comfortable being on the floor with technicians as the default operating mode.

 Experience with MES and ERP systems for production and material planning: working with JIRA, Siemens NX, Teamcenter (PLM), or Oracle or equivalents.

 Experience with Lean manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
