role.description:
**Location** Gaithersburg, Maryland, United States **Job ID** R-263851 **Date posted** 08/11/2026

 

Position Summary

The Director, Digital Twin & Intelligent Manufacturing Capabilities is responsible for defining and advancing the enterprise strategy, technology direction, governance, standards, and capability roadmap for Digital Twins, Process Twins, Process Intelligence, Modeling, Simulation, Automation-enabled Manufacturing, and AI-driven manufacturing capabilities across Global Technical Operations (GTO). This role serves as GTO's enterprise leader for Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities and is accountable for shaping how manufacturing science, process knowledge, automation, data, advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, and digital technologies are leveraged to improve technology transfer, process understanding, manufacturing readiness, operational performance, and business outcomes across the product lifecycle.

The Director will partner closely with MPAS, Tech Transfer, BPD, Singapore manufacturing and digital organizations, Alexion, FMC, Regional Digital Leads, Manufacturing, IT, Enterprise Architecture, Data & AI, Automation, and Site Digital teams to establish enterprise-scale capabilities and implementation frameworks that can be deployed consistently across the manufacturing network. While Regional Digital Leads and site organizations retain accountability for site-level deployment and adoption, this role is responsible for defining the enterprise capability strategy, technology direction, operating model, governance, standards, and reusable assets required to scale Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities across GTO.

This position requires deep expertise in Digital Twin and Intelligent Manufacturing capabilities, combined with strong technology leadership, manufacturing and process-science credibility, automation awareness, systems thinking, vendor evaluation experience, AI and advanced analytics fluency, and a proven ability to lead large-scale cross-functional transformation initiatives in complex global organizations.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Enterprise Strategy & Capability Leadership**

* Define and maintain the enterprise strategy for Digital Twins, Process Twins, Process Intelligence, Modeling, Simulation, and Intelligent Manufacturing capabilities across GTO.

* Establish and evolve a multi-year capability roadmap aligned with GTO priorities, Digital Tech Transfer strategy, manufacturing modernization initiatives, and enterprise digital objectives.

* Identify strategic opportunities to improve technology transfer, process characterization, scale-up, manufacturing readiness, process robustness, operational performance, and business value.

* Develop capability maturity models, adoption frameworks, and value realization approaches to support enterprise scaling.

* Translate business needs and manufacturing challenges into actionable capability roadmaps, standards, investment priorities, and implementation approaches.

**Technology, Automation & Intelligent Manufacturing Leadership**

* Define how Digital Twins, manufacturing systems, automation environments, process data, simulation platforms, advanced analytics, machine learning, and AI capabilities work together as part of GTO’s Intelligent Manufacturing ecosystem.

* Lead evaluation and selection of Digital Twin, Process Intelligence, Modeling, Simulation, and AI-enabled manufacturing technologies.

* Drive technology strategy and investment recommendations across platforms, tools, vendors, and strategic partnerships.

* Assess emerging technologies and industry developments to guide future capability investments and roadmap decisions.

* Partner with Enterprise Architecture, IT, Data & AI, Automation, and Digital organizations to define scalable architectures, integration approaches, and operational models.

* Establish approaches for connecting process knowledge, manufacturing systems, automation platforms, process data, simulations, and Digital Twins through effective data flows and information architectures.

* Guide build-versus-buy decisions and strategic technology direction for Digital Twin and Intelligent Manufacturing capabilities.

**Process Intelligence, Modeling & Digital Twin Governance**

* Establish governance frameworks, standards, methodologies, and best practices for Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities across GTO.

* Define and oversee model lifecycle management approaches, including model transition, deployment, maintenance, monitoring, documentation, and retirement.

* Establish ownership models, stewardship expectations, support models, and decision-making frameworks for Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities.

* Develop reusable methods, templates, and standards that enable scalability and consistency across products, sites, and manufacturing networks.

* Ensure Digital Twin and Process Intelligence initiatives are aligned to enterprise quality, regulatory, and operational expectations.

**Community of Practice & Capability Development**

* Establish and lead the GTO Digital Twin & Process Intelligence Community of Practice and Center of Excellence.

* Build and maintain a network of practitioners and subject matter experts across Manufacturing, MPAS, Tech Transfer, BPD, Automation, IT, Data & AI, Site Digital organizations, and Regional Digital Leads.

* Develop standards, reference architectures, implementation guidance, training materials, and best practices to support capability maturity and enterprise adoption.

* Promote innovation, knowledge sharing, and capability development across the organization.

* Sponsor and oversee Digital Twin and Process Intelligence initiatives involving interns, graduate students, and university partnerships aligned to strategic business priorities.

* Collaborate with academic institutions, innovation partners, and external research organizations to advance Digital Twin and Intelligent Manufacturing capabilities.

**Enterprise Transformation & Business Partnership**

* Partner closely with MPAS, Tech Transfer, BPD, Singapore manufacturing organizations, Alexion, FMC, and Manufacturing organizations to identify opportunities and shape future-state capabilities.

* Ensure Digital Twin and Process Intelligence strategies align with broader Digital Tech Transfer, Intelligent Manufacturing, and GTO transformation objectives.

* Lead complex cross-functional initiatives requiring alignment across business, scientific, manufacturing, digital, and technology organizations.

* Influence strategic decisions and drive organizational alignment without direct authority.

* Translate emerging technologies into scalable business capabilities and measurable outcomes.

**External Innovation & Vendor Management**

* Build and manage relationships with strategic technology vendors, industry organizations, academic partners, and innovation ecosystems.

* Lead technology assessments, proof-of-concept initiatives, capability evaluations, and vendor-selection activities.

* Monitor industry developments in Digital Twins, Process Intelligence, Manufacturing Analytics, Simulation, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, and Intelligent Manufacturing.

* Guide strategic partnerships and investment decisions that strengthen GTO’s long-term Digital Twin and Process Intelligence capabilities.

**Qualifications**

Required

* Advanced degree (Master’s or PhD) in Engineering, Manufacturing Systems, Chemical Engineering, Bioprocess Engineering, Data Science, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Operations Research, Life Sciences, or a related technical discipline.

* 12-20+ years of experience in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, manufacturing, engineering, automation, process development, digital transformation, or related industries.

* Demonstrated experience leading enterprise-scale Digital Twin, Process Twin, Process Intelligence, Simulation, Advanced Analytics, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, or Intelligent Manufacturing initiatives.

* Strong understanding of manufacturing systems, automation environments, industrial data flows, manufacturing data ecosystems, and Intelligent Manufacturing concepts.

* Experience evaluating technology platforms, software vendors, emerging technologies, and digital capabilities.

* Demonstrated ability to develop capability roadmaps, guide technology investments, and establish enterprise governance and standards.

* Strong understanding of AI, machine learning, advanced analytics, simulation technologies, and their practical application in manufacturing and process environments.

* Demonstrated ability to lead complex, cross-functional transformation initiatives in highly matrixed organizations.

* Proven ability to influence senior scientific, manufacturing, business, and technology stakeholders without direct authority.

* Excellent executive communication, stakeholder engagement, facilitation, and leadership skills.

**Preferred**

* Experience in biologics manufacturing, process development, manufacturing sciences, technology transfer, or technical operations.

* Experience working across BPD, MPAS, Manufacturing, Tech Transfer, Automation, IT, Data & AI, and Enterprise Architecture organizations.

* Familiarity with Digital Twin and Process Intelligence platforms such as BaseTwo, M-Star, FlexSim, BioSolve, Solvace, AspenTech, AVEVA, or similar ecosystems.

* Experience establishing enterprise communities of practice, governance models, capability-development programs, or Centers of Excellence.

**Job Description**

As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.

**LOCATION**: Currently tied to Morrisville, NC (may be open to other locations). Relocation assistance is NOT provided.

* Must be legally authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship.
* Must be able to pass a comprehensive background check, which includes a drug screening.

**DESCRIPTION**:

As a Senior Director of Operations at Thermo Fisher Scientific, you'll manage complex manufacturing operations while driving strategic growth and operational excellence. This key leadership role involves directing production of high-quality products in regulated environments while ensuring exceptional customer service and compliance. You'll optimize end-to-end operations, implement continuous improvement initiatives, and develop high-performing teams aligned with our mission of enabling customers to make the world healthier, cleaner, and safer.

Working closely with cross-functional partners, you'll establish and execute strategic plans, drive productivity and efficiency improvements, and support a culture focused on quality, safety and customer success. This role requires strong business acumen to manage P&L responsibilities while scaling operations to meet growing demand. You'll support our PPI (Practical Process Improvement) business system and 4i values - Integrity, Intensity, Innovation and Involvement - while developing talent and building engaged, collaborative teams.

**REQUIREMENTS**:

* Strong business acumen and analytical capabilities

role.title: Plant Manager
role.description:
**Pacific Coast Producers |** Full-Time | On-Site | Exempt 
**Salary Range:** $160,000- $200,000 /year (based on experience)

**Pacific Coast Producers** (PCP), a growing agricultural cooperative with food production facilities across the West Coast, is seeking an experienced and strategic **Plant Manager** to lead our Production Facility **in Lodi, CA**. PCP is dedicated to investing in its people and fostering a culture of service, where each employee can do their best to make affordable, high-quality food for customers across North America.

Join our legacy of talented people working together to innovate and lead our industry. As a member of PCP, you will have access to a comprehensive benefits package that includes top-quality, medical, dental, and vision insurance, generous paid time off, and a retirement savings plan to help secure your future.

The Plant Manager will have overall accountability for directing and managing plant operations to meet quality, food safety, and customer requirements in a safe, cost-effective, and timely manner. The plant employs over 800 employees during the processing season and maintains an experienced year-round staff. The Plant Manager reports directly to the Director of Operations.

**What You'll Do:**

* Lead all aspects of plant operations, ensuring safe, efficient, and high-quality production
* Develop and execute production plans aligned with raw material supply, demand, labor, and plant capacity
* Drive performance against key metrics including safety, quality, throughput, and cost
* Own operating and capital budgets; analyzing performance and implementing corrective actions
* Champion food safety, environmental compliance, and regulatory adherence (OSHA, FDA, SQF, HACCP, HARPC, GMPs)
* Build, coach, and develop strong teams through clear expectations and consistent leadership
* Lead continuous improvement initiatives to enhance efficiency, reliability, and profitability
* Partner effectively with union leadership to maintain a positive and productive work environment
* Oversee capital projects and internal investments to support future growth and operational excellence

**What You Bring to the Team:**

* 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in food manufacturing including aseptic processing, canning, or similar method.
* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, or related field
* Proven ability to lead large teams in a fast-paced, unionized setting
* Proven experience with process flows, automated controls, review of AutoCAD drawings, and dealing with industrial processing equipment vendors and mechanical contractors.
* Strong operational and financial acumen, including budgeting and performance analysis
* Demonstrated success driving continuous improvement and leading change
* Deep understanding of food safety systems and regulatory requirements (GFSI, HACCP, HARPC, FDA, OSHA)
* Hands-on leadership style with strong problem-solving capability
* Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results under tight timelines
* Strong communication skills with the ability to influence across all levels of the organization

**Why Join PCP?**

At PCP, we take care of our people. Here are just a few of the benefits full-time employees enjoy:

* **Competitive pay** with opportunities for advancement.
* **This position is eligible for our annual profit-sharing bonus program**.
* **Medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your family, starting the first of the month after you join us.**
* **Retirement plans** to support your long-term security.
* **Paid time off** including vacation, holidays, parental leave, sick leave, and bereavement.
* **Life and disability insurance** plus an Employee Assistance Program.
* **Development opportunities** through online courses, classroom training, and on-the-job growth.
* The stability of a **farmer-owned cooperative** with more than 50 years of success.
* A mission-driven culture focused on **feeding families across North America.**

**Salary Range: $160,000 - $200,000/year (based on experience).** This is a **full-time, on-site** role based at our production facility Lodi, CA.

The base salary range reflects the reasonable expectation for what the company anticipates paying for this role at the time of posting. The actual salary offered will depend on factors including, but not limited to:

* Relevant skills, education, and experience
* Job-related qualifications and certifications
* Internal pay equity
* Market conditions and business needs

**Sponsorship:** This role is not eligible for current or future visa sponsorship.

**About PCP Summary**

Founded in 1971, Pacific Coast Producers is owned by more than 165 family farmers who cultivate and deliver a diverse range of crops including tomatoes, peaches, pears, grapes, cherries, and more. Our cooperative operates multiple processing and packaging facilities across the West Coast, supplying top-quality products to grocery retailers and foodservice distributors throughout the U.S. and Canada.

Our Lodi Production facility is a bustling hub where delicious apples, peaches, and apricots are transformed into high-quality products. The facility is equipped with advanced machinery and cutting-edge technology, enabling efficient and precise sorting, peeling, and slicing of the fruits. Meticulous attention is paid to every step of the process, ensuring that only the finest fruits make their way into the final products.

Nestled in the heart of San Joaquin County and just a short 45-minute drive from Sacramento, our Production Facility is located in the charming city of Lodi, CA. Lodi is renowned for its rich history in winemaking and agriculture, as well as its vibrant downtown area and close-knit community. With a great quality of life, Lodi offers a welcoming environment to those seeking a relaxed and enjoyable lifestyle.

**AA/EEO Policy Statement**

Pacific Coast Producers is an affirmative action and equal opportunity employer. No employee or applicant will be discriminated against in any condition of employment because of race, color, national origin, sex, religion, age, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by law.

role.title: Sr. Manager - Quality - Visual Inspection & Particulate Control
role.description:
**Req #** 212920 **Location** Round Lake, Illinois, United States **Job Category** Quality **Date posted** 11/09/2026

 

**Overview**
------------

This is where you make a difference in our patients’ safety. As a member of the Baxter Quality team, you will play an essential part in our mission of saving and sustaining lives. Quality is important throughout the entire product lifecycle and works collaboratively with all areas of the organization. Because Quality touches everything Baxter does, a role in Quality provides many opportunities for growth, learning and a successful career that has a daily impact on people’s lives.

* Support for Parents
* Continuing Education/ Professional Development
* Employee Health & Well-Being Benefits
* Paid Time Off
* 2 Days a Year to Volunteer

**Success Profile**
-------------------

What makes a successful Quality team member at Baxter? Take a look at some of the top traits we’re looking for and see if you’re a fit.

* Detail Oriented
* Continuous Learner
* Courageous
* Collaborative
* Critical Thinker
* Influential

 

**This is where** your work makes a difference.

At Baxter, we believe every person—regardless of who they are or where they are from—deserves a chance to live a healthy life. It was our founding belief in 1931 and continues to be our guiding principle. We are redefining healthcare delivery to make a greater impact today, tomorrow, and beyond.

Our Baxter colleagues are united by our Mission to Save and Sustain Lives. Together, our community is driven by a culture of courage, trust, and collaboration. Every individual is empowered to take ownership and make a meaningful impact. We strive for efficient and effective operations, and we hold each other accountable for delivering exceptional results.

Here, you will find more than just a job—you will find purpose and pride.

**Your Role**

The Sr. Manager - Quality - Visual Inspection & Particulate Control provides strategic and technical Quality leadership for manufacturing and laboratory quality systems, with a focus on Visual Inspection and particulate matter control for injectable products. This role ensures that inspection programs, qualification/validation, particulate investigations, and associated controls are scientifically sound, risk-based, well documented, and aligned with regulatory requirements, compendial expectations, and the company Quality Management System.

**What You'll Be Doing**
------------------------

* Lead Quality oversight for manual, semi-automated, and automated visual inspection programs, ensuring inspection processes remain effective, compliant, and aligned with patient safety expectations.
* Develop and maintain risk-based particulate control strategies that strengthen defect prevention, improve manufacturing controls, and reduce product quality risks.
* Provide technical leadership for qualification and validation activities related to visual inspection systems, ensuring studies are scientifically sound, appropriately designed, and fully documented.
* Direct complex investigations involving visible particulate matter, inspection trends, and product quality events, driving objective root cause analysis and effective corrective actions.
* Partner with Operations, Engineering, Laboratory, and Quality teams to identify opportunities for process improvement, defect reduction, and continuous enhancement of inspection performance.
* Support regulatory inspections, customer audits, and health authority interactions by providing expertise, documentation, and responses related to visual inspection and particulate control programs.
* Establish and monitor quality performance metrics, trend analyses, and risk indicators to proactively identify emerging issues and ensure sustainable improvements.
 

 

**What You'll Bring**
---------------------

 
 

### **Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Pharmacy, Chemistry, Biology, Microbiology, Engineering, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related scientific or technical discipline.
* Typically 10+ years of progressive experience within pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical, medical device, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments, including significant Quality leadership responsibilities.
* Demonstrated expertise in visual inspection programs for injectable or sterile products, including inspection strategy, defect classification, qualification programs, and performance monitoring.
* Experience leading complex investigations, risk assessments, corrective and preventive action (CAPA) programs, validation activities, and regulatory inspection responses.
* Strong knowledge of current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP) and applicable compendial requirements, including USP and USP .
* Experience making science-based quality decisions involving product disposition, compliance risk management, and quality system effectiveness.
* Strong communication, collaboration, and influencing skills with the ability to build alignment across multiple functions while maintaining independent quality judgment.
* Leadership experience through direct people leadership, matrix leadership, or technical leadership roles.
 

 

### **Preferred Qualifications**

* Advanced degree in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Chemistry, Microbiology, Engineering, or a related discipline.

role.title: Sr. Manager of Engineering (Device Assembly, Labeling & Packaging)
role.description:
US - Ohio - New Albany

JOB ID: R-258401 LOCATION: US - Ohio - New Albany WORK LOCATION TYPE: On Site DATE POSTED: Nov. 09, 2026 CATEGORY: Engineering SALARY RANGE: 148,715.15USD -201,202.85 USD

**Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients**

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

 
 

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

 
 

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

 
 

**What you will do**

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this role the Senior Manager of Engineering is responsible for providing technical and engineering leadership for the design, development, implementation, qualification, and lifecycle management of pharmaceutical device assembly, labeling, and secondary and tertiary packaging process equipment.

This role requires **deep technical expertise in pharmaceutical manufacturing and packaging technologies**, combined with demonstrated industry experience delivering complex automation and equipment projects in a highly regulated environment.

 
 

The Senior Manager will lead high-visibility, cross-functional engineering initiatives from early concept and technology selection through design, equipment development, integration, qualification, operational readiness, and sustained manufacturing support. The successful candidate will work closely with Manufacturing/Operations, Quality, Automation, Validation, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Process Development, Regulatory, and external equipment suppliers to deliver robust, reliable, compliant, and scalable manufacturing solutions.

 
 

The position requires a leader who can operate effectively at both the **technical detail and strategic program level**, challenge equipment designs and technical decisions, manage complex project risks, influence stakeholders, and drive issues to resolution.

 
 

**Key Responsibilities**
------------------------

### **Engineering & Technical Leadership**

* Provide technical leadership for **device assembly, labeling, secondary packaging, and tertiary packaging equipment and automation systems**.
* Lead the assessment, selection, design, development, implementation, and lifecycle management of process technologies and equipment.
* Develop equipment and automation strategies that support manufacturing reliability, product quality, operational efficiency, flexibility, and long-term technology standardization.
* Provide technical direction through equipment concept development, design reviews, detailed engineering, equipment build, testing, installation, commissioning, qualification, and operational ramp-up.
* Critically review equipment architecture, automation concepts, control strategies, material flow, product handling, inspection systems, and machine interfaces.
* Apply strong engineering fundamentals and industry knowledge to identify technical risks early and develop effective mitigation strategies.
* Drive technical problem solving and structured root-cause analysis for complex equipment, automation, process, and reliability issues.
* Establish and promote engineering standards and best practices for equipment design, technology selection, maintainability, reliability, and lifecycle management.
 

 

### **Equipment & Technology Expertise**

The successful candidate should have demonstrated experience with technologies associated with pharmaceutical combination-product/device assembly and packaging, including several of the following:

* Automated and semi-automated medical device assembly
* Cartoning and case packing
* Product and component feeding and handling systems
* Label application and verification
* Serialization and track-and-trace technologies
* Vision and inspection systems
* Printing, coding, and marking systems
* Leaflet and booklet feeding
* Robotics and material handling
* Conveyance and product-transfer systems
* Secondary and tertiary packaging automation
* PLC/HMI and industrial automation systems
* Equipment data acquisition and manufacturing system interfaces
 

 

### **Capital Project & Program Leadership**

* Lead complex, **high-visibility engineering and capital equipment projects** involving multiple functions, suppliers, technologies, and manufacturing stakeholders.
* Translate product, process, business, and regulatory requirements into clear equipment and engineering requirements.
* Lead equipment projects through key phases including concept development, user requirements, specification, supplier selection, design reviews, FAT, SAT, commissioning, qualification, and production readiness.
* Own technical project execution while proactively managing scope, schedule, technical risk, interfaces, dependencies, and critical decisions.
* Establish clear escalation paths and communicate project status, technical risks, tradeoffs, and recommendations to senior leadership.
* Ensure technical decisions are documented and supported by appropriate engineering rationale and risk assessment.
 

 

### **Cross-Functional Leadership**

* Partner closely with **Operations, Quality, Validation, Automation, Maintenance, Process Development, Supply Chain, Regulatory, and other engineering organizations** to successfully deliver new manufacturing capabilities.
* Facilitate technical discussions and drive alignment across functions when requirements or priorities conflict.
* Build strong partnerships with manufacturing teams to ensure new technologies are operationally sustainable and successfully transitioned into routine production.
* Influence stakeholders and senior leaders without relying solely on direct authority.
* Communicate complex engineering topics clearly to both highly technical teams and executive leadership.
 

 

### **Supplier & OEM Management**

* Provide technical leadership in relationships with equipment OEMs, system integrators, automation suppliers, and engineering partners.
* Establish clear technical expectations, specifications, deliverables, design-review criteria, and acceptance requirements.
* Challenge suppliers constructively to ensure equipment solutions meet technical, quality, reliability, schedule, and operational requirements.
* Lead technical reviews and critical equipment milestones including design reviews, FATs, SATs, and performance evaluations.
* Evaluate emerging equipment and automation technologies and assess their applicability to current and future manufacturing needs.
 

 

### **People Leadership & Organizational Capability**

* Lead, develop, coach, and mentor engineers and technical professionals.
* Build engineering capability in equipment design, automation, packaging technologies, technical problem solving, and project execution.
* Establish clear expectations and accountability while creating an environment that encourages technical rigor, collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement.
* Develop internal technical expertise while effectively leveraging external OEM and engineering resources.
 

 

**Join Amgen’s Mission of Serving Patients**

At Amgen, if you feel like you’re part of something bigger, it’s because you are. Our shared mission—to serve patients living with serious illnesses—drives all that we do.

 
 

Since 1980, we’ve helped pioneer the world of biotech in our fight against the world’s toughest diseases. With our focus on four therapeutic areas –Oncology, Inflammation, General Medicine, and Rare Disease– we reach millions of patients each year. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases, and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives.

 
 

Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lay within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career.

 
 

Automation Maintenance Technician

 
 

**What you will do**

Let’s do this. Let’s change the world. In this role the Associate Mfg Systems Engineer for the new Amgen Advanced Assembly and Final Product Operation facility will be part of the Facilities & Engineering team responsible for providing automation and technical support for the safe and reliable operation of our advanced automated warehouse and automated guided vehicle systems (Automated storage and retrieval System - ASRS). You will have the exciting opportunity to support performing advanced installation, troubleshooting, maintenance, repair, testing, and documentation/logs of our advanced warehouse automation systems that require strong analytical problem-solving techniques.

 
 

Specific Responsibilities include but are not limited to:

* Strictly follow the company’s safety and cGMP policies and procedures.
* Provide operational shift support for process control applications applying Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC), Human Machine Interfaces (HMI), Variable Frequency Drives (VFD) and vision systems.
* Apply engineering principles of process automation to provide technical support to the automated warehouse, automated guided vehicles, and manufacturing production.
* Implement control system troubleshooting support for the ASRS integrated system.
* Implement automated process changes to improved equipment performance or upgraded equipment technologies.
* Participate in technical root cause analysis, incident investigations, and troubleshooting on automation control issues related to electrical, instrumentation, and control systems.
* Perform required work in a GMP regulated manufacturing setting.
* Implement Preventative and Corrective maintenance.
* Ensure strict adherence to Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) and maintain accurate GMP documentation following ALCOA+ principles.
* Support project management efforts for automation-related projects.
* Handle Automation Systems lifecycle including controlled changes, software versioning, and control system qualification. Ensure all changes are properly documented and approved.
* Support Data Integrity Assessments.
* Maintain automated warehouse systems applying Allen Bradley Programmable Logic Controllers (PLC), Human Machine Interfaces (HMI) and Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition systems (SCADA).
* Support Continuous Improvement initiatives including Safety, Reliability, Efficiency and Environmental sustainability improvements to meet Amgen’s goals.
* Business Process Improvements including departmental Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) and Job plans for the area of responsibility to assure all maintenance operations are performed safely and reliably.

**What we expect of you**

We are all different, yet we all use our unique contributions to serve patients. The professional we seek will possess these qualifications.

 
 

**Basic Qualifications:**
-------------------------

Doctorate degree and 2 years of **Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation/Controls Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Packaging Engineering**, or a related technical discipline experience

OR

Master’s degree and 6 years of **Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation/Controls Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Packaging Engineering**, or a related technical discipline experience

OR

Bachelor’s degree and 8 years of **Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation/Controls Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Packaging Engineering**, or a related technical discipline experience

OR

Associate’s degree and 10 years of **Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation/Controls Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Packaging Engineering**, or a related technical discipline experience

OR

High school diploma / GED and 12 years of **Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation/Controls Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Packaging Engineering**, or a related technical discipline experience

 
 

In addition to meeting at least one of the above requirements, you must have a minimum of 2 years experience directly managing people and/or leadership experience leading teams, projects, programs, or directing the allocation or resources. Your managerial experience may run concurrently with the required technical experience referenced above

 
 

**Preferred Qualifications**
----------------------------

* Bachelor’s degree in **Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Automation/Controls Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Packaging Engineering**, or a related technical discipline.
* Significant engineering experience within the **pharmaceutical, biotechnology, medical device, combination-product, or other highly regulated manufacturing industry**.
* Demonstrated experience with **secondary and tertiary packaging, labeling, and/or automated device assembly equipment**.
* Strong experience leading the **design, development, implementation, commissioning, and qualification of automated process equipment**.
* Demonstrated leadership of complex, high-visibility capital or equipment projects involving multiple cross-functional organizations.
* Experience working directly with equipment OEMs, automation suppliers, system integrators, and engineering partners.
* Working knowledge of regulated manufacturing environments and applicable GMP/GxP principles.
* Demonstrated ability to lead technical investigations and resolve complex equipment and manufacturing problems.
* Strong technical communication, leadership, stakeholder-management, and decision-making skills.

**What you can expect from us**
-------------------------------

As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. From our competitive benefits to our collaborative culture, we’ll support your journey every step of the way.

 
 

The expected annual salary range for this role in the U.S. (excluding Puerto Rico) is posted. Actual salary will vary based on several factors including but not limited to, relevant skills, experience, and qualifications.

 
 

In addition to the base salary, Amgen offers a Total Rewards Plan, based on eligibility, comprising of health and welfare plans for staff and eligible dependents, financial plans with opportunities to save towards retirement or other goals, work/life balance, and career development opportunities that may include:

* A comprehensive employee benefits package, including a Retirement and Savings Plan with generous company contributions, group medical, dental and vision coverage, life and disability insurance, and flexible spending accounts
* A discretionary annual bonus program, or for field sales representatives, a sales-based incentive plan
* Stock-based long-term incentives
* Award-winning time-off plans
* Flexible work models, including remote and hybrid work arrangements, where possible

 

**for a career that defies imagination**

Objects in your future are closer than they appear. Join us.

**careers.amgen.com**

 
 

**Sponsorship**
---------------

Sponsorship for this role is not guaranteed.

 
 

In any materials you submit, you may redact or remove age-identifying information such as age, date of birth, or dates of school attendance or graduation. You will not be penalized for redacting or removing this information.

 
 

As an organization dedicated to improving the quality of life for people around the world, Amgen fosters an inclusive environment of diverse, ethical, committed and highly accomplished people who respect each other and live the Amgen values to continue advancing science to serve patients. Together, we compete in the fight against serious disease.

 
 

Amgen is an Equal Opportunity employer and will consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status, or any other basis protected by applicable law.

 
 

We will ensure that individuals with disabilities are provided reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, to perform essential job functions, and to receive other benefits and privileges of employment. Please contact us to request accommodation.

role.title: Director, Operational Excellence
role.description:
The Director, Operational Excellence, is a hands-on practitioner who supports ESCO sites in deploying the **ESCO Operating System (EOS)**. The person in this role travels to sites to facilitate Kaizen events, take part in key EOS activities, and coach site leaders and teams to strengthen EOS adoption, practice, and results.

Site Presidents and site EOS Managers own and lead EOS deployment at their sites. This role supports them as an experienced practitioner and member of a small central EOS team. The EOS Program Lead owns program strategy and the development of EOS elements, and a peer role owns data, tools, KPIs, and monthly business reviews. This role helps sites put EOS standards into practice on the floor and brings field learning back to improve those standards.

This is a director-level individual contributor role with no direct reports. It works through influence with site leaders and teams. The initial focus is the Aerospace & Defense group, with expansion to other ESCO divisions as EOS deployment grows.

**Key Responsibilities**

***Site Deployment Support***

* Support site Presidents and EOS Managers in executing their annual EOS deployment plans toward EOS maturity certifications.
* Participate in key EOS activities during site visits, such as MDI, Kaizen events, and Gemba Walks, and provide sites with direct feedback to enhance adoption and practice.
* Help sites put EOS elements into practice, including MDI, Gemba Walks, KPI management, action management, P&R, structured problem solving, and leader standard work.
* Provide sites with continued support to improve EOS adoption, sustainment, and results.

***Kaizen and Improvement Events***

* Plan and facilitate Kaizen events with site teams: scoping and chartering with site leadership, pre-event data collection, team training, current state analysis, implementation on the floor, report-out, and 30/60/90-day follow-up.
* Help sites build and manage their CI pipeline so events are selected based on business priorities, KPI gaps, and financial impact.
* Develop site Kaizen leaders and facilitators so sites can run events on their own and meet their annual Kaizen plan.
* Document event results and savings, and partner with site finance to validate benefits.

***Coaching and Capability Building***

* Deliver EOS training on site, from leadership sessions to hands-on floor training for supervisors and team members.
* Coach site leaders, supervisors, and EOS Managers on daily management, visual management, standard work, and problem solving.
* Support site EOS Managers in developing EOS champions and practitioners at their sites.

***Assessment, Tracking, and Feedback***

* Support EOS maturity assessments and certification readiness reviews, including site tours, interviews, and evidence review.
* Monitor deployment progress, action closure, and sustainment at supported sites, and report status to the EOS Program Lead.
* Help site leaders remove barriers, and raise issues to the EOS Program Lead when deployment is at risk.
* Bring field feedback into the EOS program: what works, what does not, and where process guides, tools, and training need to change.
* Share good practices across sites and connect site teams with each other.

**Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Supply Chain, or related field required.
* 8+ years of experience in operational excellence, continuous improvement, Lean, or manufacturing operations, including at least 5 years in a hands-on deployment or practitioner role.
* Has personally facilitated 10 - 20 or more Kaizen events with documented results.
* Hands-on experience practicing and coaching tiered daily management (MDI or similar), Gemba Walks, visual management, standard work, and structured problem solving (A3, PDCA, root cause analysis).
* Experience in a company with a structured operating or business system strongly preferred. Must be a U.S. Person and able to provide appropriate documentation
* Experience supporting deployment across multiple sites preferred.
* Plant or operations leadership experience preferred. Credibility with site leaders and on the floor is essential.
* Aerospace, defense, industrial, or complex high-mix manufacturing experience preferred.
* Lean, Kaizen, or Six Sigma certification preferred.
* Must be a U.S. Person with a valid US passport with the ability to travel internationally.

**Required Capabilities**

* Practitioner first: comfortable on the shop floor and leading teams through hands-on change.
* Strong event facilitation, with the ability to lead mixed teams from operators to executives.
* Direct, constructive coaching of leaders at all levels, including senior leaders.
* Business acumen: connects improvement work to KPIs, EBIT, and customer commitments.
* Ability to adapt to sites at different maturity levels without lowering the standard.
* Ability to influence without direct authority.
* Self-directed and organized; manages a multi-site schedule with limited supervision.
* High accountability for follow-through and sustainment.

**Travel**

Expected travel of approximately **60% to 80%**, primarily domestic, with some international travel to sites in Mexico and the UK. A typical site visit runs 3 to 5 days, such as a Kaizen event week or a site support visit covering MDI, Gemba Walks, and other EOS activities. Candidates should be based near a major airport.

**Compensation Information** 
Base Salary Range: $190,000 - $220,000 USD (Annually)

**Actual base salary offered to the hired applicant will be determined based on their work location, level, qualifications, job related skills, as well as relevant education or training experience.**

Equal Opportunity Employer

role.title: Director of Protective Operations and Logistics
role.description:
**Fidelity will not provide immigration sponsorship for this position.**

### **Job Description:**

Director, Executive Protection, Protective Operations and Logistics

The Role:

As the Director of Protective Operations and Logistics within the Executive Protection team, you will be responsible for executive protection program management and logistical planning, including staffing, scheduling*,* protective transportation operations, support request vetting and assessment, training administration, and oversight of the TSA Aircraft Security Officer (ASO) program. Reporting to the Head of Executive Protection, you will provide operational leadership, program oversight, and subject matter expertise on executive protection and protective operations matters. You willbe responsible for ensuring the effective execution of day-to-day protective operations while supporting the continued enhancement of the firm's executive protection capabilities. The position requires close collaboration with Global Security Operations, the Global Security Operations Center (GSOC), Travel Security, and key internal and external partners to implement and support Fidelity's executive protection strategy. Success in this role requires exceptional organizational, leadership, and relationship-management skills, as well as the ability to balance competing priorities while delivering consistent, discreet, and service-oriented experience for Fidelity's senior leadership.

The Expertise and Skills You Bring

* 7-10 years of experience protecting C-suite executives, board members, and/or government officials in complex, dynamic, and globally distributed operating environments within corporate, government, military, or law enforcement settings.
* Exceptional organizational and project management skills with the ability to effectively manage multiple workstreams
* Exceptional verbal, written, and presentation skills, including the ability to communicate effectively with executives, business leaders, security professionals, and external stakeholders
* Extensive knowledge of executive protection operations, including protective advances, travel security, transportation security, venue assessment, route planning and protective operations logistics.
* Expertise in assessing, prioritizing, and coordinating executive support requests while balancing risk, resource requirements, and business priorities.
* Ability to travel domestically and internationally as required and operate effectively in dynamic, rapidly changing, and high-pressure environments.
* Strong understanding of TSA Aircraft Security Officer (ASO) program requirements, administration, compliance, certifications, and operational integration; the ability to obtain and maintain ASO certification is highly preferred.
* Demonstrated ability to manage executive protection staffing models, personnel scheduling, resource allocation, and operational readiness across multiple locations and priorities.
* Demonstrated ability to lead, mentor, develop, and build high-performing teams while fostering a culture of professionalism, accountability, discretion, and service excellence.
* Experience coordinating and supporting executive travel, special events, corporate meetings, and other high-visibility engagements requiring detailed planning and collaboration.
* Experience managing executive transportation programs, including vehicle operations, driver standards, fleet utilization, and transportation security protocols.
* Experience developing and managing executive protection training programs, operational exercises, performance standards, readiness assessments, and professional development initiatives.
* Bachelor's degree is preferred; equivalent professional experience will be considered.
* Relevant professional certifications such as CTM, CPP, PSP, ASIS Executive Protection Professional (EPP), TSA ASO, or other intelligence, investigation, or executive protection credentials are a plus.
* undefined

The Purpose of Your Role

 

* Lead the planning, coordination, and execution of executive protection programs that ensure the safety, privacy, and operational effectiveness of Fidelity's executive leadership.
* Manage the day-to-day administration and logistical support of executive protection operations, including staffing, scheduling, executive travel, protective transportation, training, and resource allocation.
* Provide operational leadership and oversight for executive protection program management, ensuring consistent service delivery, operational readiness, and alignment with organizational priorities.
* Serve as a trusted partner to executive stakeholders by delivering responsive, discreet, and customer-focused protective services in support of business activities and executive requirements.
* Oversee the planning and coordination of executive travel, special events, site visits, and high-profile engagements, ensuring appropriate protective measures and logistical support are in place.
* Manage and enhance the TSA Aircraft Security Officer (ASO) program, executive transportation services, training initiatives, and other core executive protection capabilities.
* Serve as a trusted security advisor to senior executives, providing strategic guidance, risk-based recommendations, and executive-level briefings on protective operations, emerging threats, and security-related matters.

The Team

The Executive Protection team is part of the broader Protective Services team, which in turn is part of Fidelity’s Global Security team. The Executive Protection team is a highly valued team dedicated to the protection of the firm’s executive leadership and events.

Please be advised that Fidelity’s business is governed by the provisions of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, the Investment Company Act of 1940, ERISA, numerous state laws governing securities, investment and retirement-related financial activities and the rules and regulations of numerous self-regulatory organizations, including FINRA, among others. Those laws and regulations may restrict Fidelity from hiring and/or associating with individuals with certain Criminal Histories.

Fidelity’s Onsite Working Model 
Fidelity is transitioning to a full-time onsite working model through a phased rollout across regions and roles. Currently, some roles and locations require 100% onsite presence, while others require less. Onsite expectations are likely to evolve as the rollout continues. This transition does not apply to fully remote roles.

The base salary range for this position is $95,000-186,000 USD per year.

Placement in the range will vary based on job responsibilities and scope, geographic location, candidate’s relevant experience, and other factors.

Base salary is only part of the total compensation package. Depending on the position and eligibility requirements, the offer package may also include bonus or other variable compensation.

We offer a wide range of benefits to meet your evolving needs and help you live your best life at work and at home. These benefits include comprehensive health care coverage and emotional well-being support, market-leading retirement, generous paid time off and parental leave, charitable giving employee match program, and educational assistance including student loan repayment, tuition reimbursement, and learning resources to develop your career. Note, the application window closes when the position is filled or unposted.

Please be advised that Fidelity’s business is governed by the provisions of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, the Investment Company Act of 1940, ERISA, numerous state laws governing securities, investment and retirement-related financial activities and the rules and regulations of numerous self-regulatory organizations, including FINRA, among others. Those laws and regulations may restrict Fidelity from hiring and/or associating with individuals with certain Criminal Histories.
